0.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
0.title: Introduction to DealforceCRE
0.text: What is DealforceCRE? DealforceCRE is a “Commercial Real Estate Development Software.” DealforceCRE gives commercial real estate developers the ability to manage all aspects of their development projects. So at its core, DealforceCRE is a company wide Real Estate Development Program, but it is much more than that. It is also: Task Management SystemProject Management ToolCommunication Tool Customer / Client DirectoryFile Management System Budget toolPay ApplicationsConstruction Change OrdersAnd so much more!How it works / How to use itDealforceCRE is a web-based application, so it does require the internet to use. There is nothing to install on your computer. You can access it from any computer via a web browser. DealforceCRE is built using responsive design, which means the website scales perfectly on any device. Therefore, you don't install an app on your phone or tablet to use DealforceCRE, you simply access the program via a web browser, the same way you would on your desktop or laptop computer. DealforceCRE works much like modern social media platforms, in that every user has their own login and profile. And since everyone has their own login, users have a personalized experience in DealforceCRE. One of the great features of DealforceCRE is the in-app notification system. When relevant actions occur in DealforceCRE, such as someone assigning a task to you, you receive a notification. This in-app notification system helps to greatly reduce email correspondence. Another fundamental feature of DealforceCRE is that the system is centered around Box technology. Box is a cloud storage system, which has been integrated into the DealforceCRE platform. All of your companies files move to the cloud, and then you can access your files from DealforceCRE.

1.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
1.title: Navigating DealforceCRE
1.text: Navigating DealforceCREThere are a lot of different sections in DealforceCRE. Let's try to simplify this by first understanding the main navigation areas. You have two primary navigation sections: the top header bar, and the side toolbar. Top Header BarIn this top header bar, there are a few options. 1). Search ToolsFirst, you have your project search tool, which allows you to quickly find a project. Clicking on Projects Only brings up additional options to search within a specific project or throughout the entire app.2). Admin SettingsNot all users can access this option as it is permission-based. Those that do, will be able to access the "Users" and "Lists & Tools" areas.3). Profile SettingsNext, is your username link, which allows you to adjust your profile settings. These user settings are broken down into two categories. General Profile SettingsThis section is where you would set your email, name, password, and profile image. Notification SettingsFrom this page, you can choose whether you receive specific notifications in-app, and/or in email, and/or in a daily aggregated email (Daily Digest). By default, new users have all of their in-app and email notifications turned on. You can adjust these and turn some off if needed, but as a general rule of thumb, at the very least, you should have either in-app OR email turned on for possible notification. 4). Help IconClicking this icon will allow the user to view our Trainual documentation or submit a ticket to our support department.5). Notification Alert / Bell This section is directly tied to your notification settings. Any time you have a a red box with a number here, this means some action has taken place that requires your attention. Clicking the bell will show you these notifications. 6). Logout Clicking this button logs you out of DealforceCRE.

2.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
2.title: Project Navigation
2.text: Project NavigationUnderstanding the DealforceCRE layout can be summarized as this: You are either looking at a specific project, or you are looking at global details across all projects. Where users collectively spend the most time in DealforceCRE is inside specific projects. You can tell when you are looking at a specific project by its tab layout. This will likely be the view / section of DealforceCRE that you become most familiar with. 1). Opening a ProjectTo get to the project view, you have to select a specific project. The easiest way to do this is to head to the project search field in the top navigation bar and begin typing in a project name. When you find the project you would like to work on, simply click the project name in the search results.Alternatively, you can search by the project ID if you know that. This can be viewed in the menu bar of a project, and also in the URL bar. In this case, the project ID is 156. If this is typed into the DealforceCRE search bar, the "Barrow, AK- Pizza Hut" project will be pulled up.2). Project ViewAs mentioned, this project view is the most common area where users work. You will notice that there are many tabs on a project. The tabs shown will depend on the permissions set for the user that is logged in. Most of these tabs should be available to all internal users, though there are certainly going to be cases where groups of users are not seeing certain tabs, (i.e., the cash flow tab is probably only going to be viewable by select accounting personnel). The nature of these tabs can be broken down into two categories:Company-wide tabsDepartment specific tabsCompany Wide TabsThe following tabs are more company-wide and typically used by everyone: Updates Tab - high-level overview of a project, pictures, latest activity and meeting notes. Files tab - Entire file system for just this project. Schedule tab - Timeline of the project as a whole. Contacts tab - List of contacts specific to this project. Department Specific TabsThe remainder of the tabs essentially represent the different departments of your organization, (e.g. construction tab, marketing tab).Very few users probably know (or need to know) what is in all of the other tabs. Your marketing team will probably only be working in the marketing tab, the sales team will probably only be in the sales tab. **Side Note: There are many differences and similarities between each tab. But one important thing to note is that many of these tabs have 'Todos Lists.' You will learn more about Todos in another module. But for now, just realize that these are common checklists, that you'll find on most tabs. The important takeaway here is that you understand what to do if someone says, "go into the Tempe, AZ - Test project schedule." You should now to know to search for the Tempe, AZ - Test Project, and then from the Project View, you click on the corresponding tab.

3.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
3.title: Global Navigation
3.text: Global NavigationWe just showed you all the basics of navigating a specific project. But what about when you want to look at information across all projects, or just view information on a higher level?That's where the global navigation comes in. The Global Navigation has many of the same features/tools that you have seen in a specific project view. The difference is, when accessing these tools from global navigation, you're looking at these features across all projects as opposed to just one project.The purpose of this training module is not to show you what happens when you click on every single global navigation link, but rather, to give you a few examples to show you how they are different from viewing more specific information inside a particular project. The following highlights the differences between using a feature in a project and using the same feature in global navigation. Example 1 - Schedule Project - Clicking the schedule in a project shows only that project's schedule. See image belowGlobal - Clicking the global schedule link in global navigation shows you schedule items across all projects. Example 2 - Contacts Project - Clicking the contacts tab in a project shows only that project's contacts. See image belowGlobal - Clicking the global contacts link in global navigation shows contacts across all projects. The rest of these global navigation links work the same way. When you click one, you're viewing that feature/information across all projects.

4.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
4.title: Logging into DealforceCRE
4.text: 1. Before signing in, one of the DealforceCRE users will add you to the system, and you will receive an email invitation to set up your account. See a sample email below.Subject: Invitation InstructionsHello USER,INTERNAL USER has invited you to www.<<companyname>>.dealforcecre.com, you can accept it through the link below.Accept Invitation [linked]This invitation will expire on DATE. If you don't want to accept the invitation, please ignore this email. Your account won't be created until you access the link above and set your password.Thanks, Your Team at <<companyname>>2. Once you click the link, you'll be taken to a page to set your password.3. You will then be signed in and ready to complete the rest of your account.4. To sign in once your account is setup, navigate to your companies DealforceCRE URL. To make signing in quick, save this as a bookmark in your toolbar!

5.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
5.title: Add your personal details
5.text: 1. To edit your profile, click on your name or profile picture in the upper right hand corner of the screen.2. From here you can update settings such as your Meeting task list, your default project tab, change your password and update your profile picture. Click 'Save & Next' to move onto the Notification Preference tab.

6.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
6.title: Customize your notification preferences
6.text: 1. Navigate to your profile and then click 'Save & Next' to move onto the Notification Preferences tab.2. Under the Notification Preferences, you have the option to choose from In-App, Email, and Daily Digest notifications. You can choose one, none (but we don't recommend it), or all of them! It's up to you. In-App - Immediate notifications that appear by the bell in the top right-hand corner of the screen with a little red number iconEmail - Immediate email notifications to your inboxDaily Digest - Daily overnight email with a recap of all the notifications from the previous day3. Click 'Save' and you're good to go!

7.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
7.title: Download Box Drive
7.text: To download Box Drive, follow these instructions:1. Click here to visit the Box Drive download page. Note: If you are a current Box user with "Box Sync" access, you'll need to uninstall Sync first.2. Select whether you have a Windows or Mac computer. Note that you'll need at least Windows 7 to run Box Drive3. Download the DMG file and run the installer, if installing on MacOS. On a Windows machine, open the .exe file to begin the installation:4. Once installed, you'll be asked to use your login credentials. If you don't have login credentials, email whoever is in charge of inviting and managing DealforceCRE users within your organization (your internal DealforceCRE administrator). You should have received an email from Box asking you to create a login if your account was set up correctly.5. You will now see Box Drive in your Finder (Mac) or Explorer (Windows).

8.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
8.title: Using Box Drive
8.text: Think of Box Drive as another method to access files on DealforceCRE. Box allows you to access files via the cloud. When you want to download, upload, delete, or edit a folder or file, you can choose to sign in to DealforceCRE or use Box Drive.Box Drive Tips and Tricks Search for folders and files by using Finder (Mac) or Explorer (Windows). You can also click the Box icon in your navigation bar to quick-search.You'll have a Box login, but it's strongly suggested you only use Box Drive or DealforceCRE to upload and manage.Box Drive does not automatically download your files and folders. It's simply a tool you can use to manage folders when connected to the internet. Files with a cloud next to them, mean that you are accessing that file/folder via the cloud.For most folders and files, having them accessible via the cloud (aka the internet) will suffice. However, you may want to save an entire folder or file to your computer. Updates to the file made by any other DealforceCRE user will still automatically update your file. But if you lose internet connection, you'll be able to still access the folder or file.To make a folder available for offline use, right-click the folder and click "Make Available Offline". You'll now see a green checkmark next to that folder/file.

9.subject: DealforceCRE - Getting Started
9.title: Adding New Users From Project
9.text: There are numerous reasons to invite external users to collaborate with you in DealforceCRE. External users can be set up with limited access and permissions to project data, allowing for an easy and centralized collaboration space between you and anyone else you're conducting business with on a project. New external users may be added through the global settings 'Directory', or through a specific project. To add new external users, you need to have the permission required to add users:'External User Access' under Project Permissions must be set to Read/WriteInternal users must have access to All Projects or Selected Projects1. Visit the project where you wish to invite an external collaborator and click the 'Contacts' tab2. Click the 'Add Contact' button and either choose the contact from the dropdown or click the 'New Contact' button and enter the information for the new External User. Note that the email must be unique, so if you have already added this user to the app for another project, select the user from the dropdown instead and skip to step 5.Enter all of the external user's information, including:Contact NameCompany (if their company is not in the list, you must create one first by clicking the New Company button)Address/Email Address/Phone Number3. Once they have been added, you will need to adjust their permissions. To do this, click their name in the Contact List.In the Edit Contact screen, in the permissions tab, click the toggle under App Access to allow them to log in to the app.After clicking the toggle, the 'Grant App Access' screen will come up. Make sure an email address and company name have been entered. Then, either choose a pre-existing department or select the radio buttons that apply to this user under the various permissions. When complete, click 'Grant App Access'.4. After giving the user access, the 'App Access' area will now show 'Granted' and you will be able to set their 'Global' and 'Project Permissions' by clicking the corresponding pencil icon.5. Now that the permissions are set, navigate back to the 'Contacts' tab within your project and verify that the 'Project Access' toggle is on so they can access that project.6. Once added to the project, the new external user will receive an email invitation, which gives them 5 days to accept. If the user is already registered with DealforceCRE, they will not receive this email.Hello [External User's Name][Internal User] has invited you to DealforceCRE, you can accept it through the link below.[ACCEPT INVITATION LINK]This invitation will expire on [date and time 5 days from today]. If you don't want to accept the invitation, please ignore this email. Your account won't be created until you access the link above and set your password.Thanks, DealforceCRE7. The External User now has access to the project's pages allowed by the role they were given when invited.

11.title: Add project overview information and update color-coded statuses

12.subject: Getting Familiar with DealforceCRE
12.title: Add and edit Contacts
12.text: 1. Navigate to the global menu and click Directory, and then click Contacts. This will bring up the entire list of Contacts for your organization.2. To add a new contact, first use the search bar to see if the contact is already in the system. If not, click the Add Contact button in the top right hand corner below your user name.3. Complete the Add Contact form as completely as possible. Make sure there aren't any typos or errors that may cause duplication in the future. 4. When you assign a Company to the Contact, be sure to search if the company already exists in the system. If not, click New Company and add the Company to the system.5. Click Save and you have successfully added a new Contact.6. To edit an existing Contact, navigate to the Directory, click on the pencil icon and make any necessary changes.

13.subject: Getting Familiar with DealforceCRE
13.title: Add and edit Companies
13.text: 1. Navigate to the global menu and click Directory, and then click Companies. This will bring up the entire list of Companies for your organization.2. To add a new company, first use the search bar to see if the company is already in the system. If not, click the Add Company button in the top right hand corner below your user name.3. Complete the Add Company form as completely as possible. Make sure there aren't any typos or errors that may cause duplication in the future. 4. Click Save and you have successfully added a new Company.5. To edit an existing Company, navigate to the Directory, click on the pencil icon and make any necessary changes.

14.subject: Getting Familiar with DealforceCRE
14.title: Add and edit Entities
14.text: The Global Entities list is nested within Directory > Entities, found in the Global Menu on the left. Click 'Add Entity' to add a new Entity.In the Add Entity screen, the Entity Name and Status are both required fields. The Status defaults to Unavailable, but can be changed at any time.After saving, the new entity will show in the list. Clicking the Entity Name will bring up the Entity Detail screen. Entities can also be edited or deleted by clicking on the corresponding icons.In order to assign an Entity to a Project, click the Edit icon that appears when you hover your cursor over the entity. Type the project name or location into the Projects field and select the project. Note: You can assign only one project to an Entity, and one Entity to a project. If you attempt to link 2, you'll have to include a justification for multiple projects (Split Parcel, or Rule 1031).After linking a project, the Status will now show Assigned and the chosen Project will appear below the status.A specific entity can be searched for in the Search bar. This screen also has options for filtering by status and all columns are sortable. There is also a Download button available that will export a .csv file with all of the entity information.

15.subject: Getting Familiar with DealforceCRE
15.title: Add and edit Tenants
15.text: Adding tenants is within the Companies directory because technically all tenants are Companies.Tenants can be added by going to Directory > Companies from the Global Menu on the left. From here, you'll want to select the company that you want to add a tenant to. You'll do that by searching for the specific company, and then selecting it's name.Once you pull up the company page, you'll want to click on the 'View Trade Name' button near the top right of the screen.The next screen looks similar, except now there's a button that says 'Add Company'. Click that.The below screen comes up, allowing you to add all needed details for the tenant. An important step here is to ensure you check the 'Tenant' box next to the company name. You will also want to ensure you have the correct 'Company Trade Name' selected. This is the company that the tenant is part of. Fill out all needed fields and press save at the bottom of the pop-up.Once you complete these steps, you'll be taken back to the main Company Trade Name screen with a list of companies associated and their status as tenants.Clicking the Tenant Name will bring up the Tenant/Company Profile Summary screen. Clicking the 'View Trade Name' button will allow you to see what company the selected company is a tenant of, or if that company has tenants or other companies (such as vendors) assigned to it. Clicking the 'Edit Company' button will allow you to edit the details of the Tenant/Company profile.

16.subject: Getting Familiar with DealforceCRE
16.title: Create a new report
16.text: 1. To navigate to the reports section to create a new report, click Reports in the left navigation and then Report Builder.2. To build a new report, first enter a Report Name. By default, the Project field is always the first column on reports created through Report Builder. You have two options for how to add additional fields. The first option is to navigate through the various categories by clicking the arrow, and then clicking the plus sign next to the fields you would like to add. The other option is to use the Search field. As you type in this field, the available fields below will update to show only those fields that include the text that you have entered.3. Click Save in the top right hand corner. This will open up your report in a table within DealforceCRE. The report will also be listed under your Reports tab on the left hand side.

17.subject: Getting Familiar with DealforceCRE
17.title: Edit existing reports
17.text: 1. To navigate to the reports section to create a new report, click Reports in the left navigation and then the report name you would like to view or edit.2. Clickto navigate back to the original report builder to add or remove fields. Click Save once the fields have been updated, or the trash icon to delete the report.3. To filter your report further, add filters such as the Project Status, City or other filters. Be sure to click the search icon to apply the filter and click Save Changes. 4. These report settings will be saved and available if you navigate back to the report later on.

18.subject: Two-Factor Authentication
18.title: Setup Two-Factor Authentication
18.text: Two-Factor Authentication (also known as 2FA or MFA) is a quick and easy way to ensure the data for your company is secure. It is called Two-Factor Authentication because you are presenting two different ways to confirm you are who you say you are: a password, and a special generated code that only the authentication integration knows. Please read the following to set up Two-Factor Authentication.Step 1:From any part of DealforceCRE, navigate to your account settings. These can be found by clicking your name in the top right corner of your window, and then clicking "Account".Step 2: Scroll down to the bottom of the account into window, and click on the button that says "Enable Two-Factor Authentication". Step 3:Here, you will have to download an authentication app to scan the QR code with. This app is what you will use to authenticate with DealforceCRE and receive a unique code to log into DealforceCRE. We recommend the app "Google Authenticator". It is available on both the Apple App Store and the Google Play Store.Step 4: Once downloaded and opened, you'll see a multicolored "+" button on the bottom right of the app. Tap this, and then scan the QR code that is shown within the DealforceCRE Two-Factor Authentication modal. When you scan this QR code from within your authenticator app, you will see DealforceCRE on the list of apps using Two-Factor Authentication. You will also see a 6 digit code. Enter this code into the "Verification Code" section on DealforceCRE. Ensure you also have your current password entered in the "Current Password" field. Then, click on "Enable Two-Factor Authentication". Step 5: The next step will show you a list of codes. You should copy & paste these into a safe place, like a Word document you won't lose, or your notes. These are one use codes that allow you to get back into your DealforceCRE account if you do not have your phone to get a 2-Factor Authentication code. Step 6:You're done! Two-Factor Authentication is now set up with your DealforceCRE account.You can disable this at any time from the same account settings. Only this time you will click "Disable Two-Factor Authentication".You will have to enter your current DealforceCRE password to confirm you'd like to disable Two-Factor Authentication.

19.subject: Workflows for Users
19.title: Overview of Workflows
19.text: From a technical standpoint, Workflows are process, communication, and notification automations in DealflorceCRE. Simply put, Workflows are background processes that ensure users aren't weighed down by cumbersome, repetitive actions within DealforceCRE. Workflows can also help to alert a user on a specific change or addition to a project within DealforceCRE, cutting down on time hunting down information. Workflows is able to do this because of things called 'Triggers' and 'Actions'. Triggers being something that happened, and the Action being what happens because of the Trigger.For example:The status of a project might change in a project -- from development to construction. The Workflow would be responsible of notifying the interested parties that the project status has changed. In that case, you or an administrator would set up a Workflow that looks something like this:These are the current Triggers and Actions available in DealforceCRE (updated 07/08/2021):Triggers:Budget ApprovedChecklist CompletedDraw Status UpdatedFile LinkedKey Date CompletedKey Date UpdatedPay App CreatedPay App Status UpdatedProject Status UpdatedTag is UsedTodo CompletedTodo List CompletedTodo Status UpdatedActions:Alert UserArchive ProjectAssign TodoChange Project HealthChange Project StatusCreate Schedule ItemQuestions:Draw StatusPay App StatusProject StatusTodo Completed

20.subject: Workflows for Users
20.title: The Technical - What does this Workflow look like?
20.text: Throughout the commercial real estate field, you are constantly tracking key dates such as Estimated Sale Date, Lease Renewals, and Award Dates. These dates, and others, are often subject to change. It can get complicated keeping track of the changes, especially having to keep track manually. With Workflows, you no longer have to do the work! You can set up a Workflow that will alert any user within DealfoceCRE when a particular key date changes.To set this up, speak with an administrator that has the ability to create Workflows.Depending on how many key dates you'd like to have a notification triggered on, the Workflow will look something like this:As you can see, there are 2 'Key Date Updated' triggers that lead to 'Alert User', and a 'Key Date Completed' trigger that leads to the user as well. That user can be set as you, or anyone else.You can ask to have a notification triggered for any key date within your instance of DealforceCRE.

21.subject: Workflows for Users
21.title: The Effect - What does this Workflow do?
21.text: You might be wondering: the Workflow has been set up by an administrator, what are the alerts going to look like? Will it be obvious?The answer is yes! Below is a demonstration of how these alerts are presented to you, the user!Let's say the previous Workflow has been triggered because the 'Award Date' has been changed within a project. You have chosen to be notified of the change. Let's take a look at what those alerts look like. In this example, the Award Date was changed. The first kind of alert that a user will receive is within their notifications section of DealforceCRE. A red circle will appear next to the bell icon, which indicates that a notification has been issued to you. When you click it, you'll see that the Workflow alert is present.When you click the alert, it'll take you to the item that triggered the Workflow. In this case, the 'Award Date' section of the schedule will come up.In addition to an in-app notification, you will also receive the below email notification. Clicking it will take you to the schedule. As you can see, there is a large amount of value added to this Workflow. It automates the process of keeping track of these key dates so that you can focus on more important tasks. In the next Workflows topic, you'll learn about tracking inactivity for things like Todo's and Pay Apps.

22.subject: Workflows for Users
22.title: The Technical - What does this Workflow look like?
22.text: As a user of DealforceCRE, you have the ability to assign Todo's to yourself or others, and followers. You also have the ability to set reminders, and alert all followers if a Todo isn't completed. However, you may want to be alerted if a Todo isn't completed by a specific date - say half to the due date, or after the due date. Or perhaps you'd like a user that's not on the Todo to be notified that the Todo is, or is not completed. That's where Workflows comes in!To set this up, speak with an administrator that has the ability to create Workflows.This looks complex - and it is - but thankfully, the administrator is who sets this up. Basically, the Workflow will have a delay attached to it. If the Todo isn't completed by a certain amount of 'delay', or time, a specified user is notified. At the same time, if a todo status is changed to completed, a specified user will be notified.This Workflow will only work for Todo's with specific key words in it - basically, tell the administrator what Todo you'd like to be notified on, and they'll ensure it's correctly chosen.Enough of the technical - let's take a look at the effect of this Workflow!

23.subject: Workflows for Users
23.title: The Effect - What does this Workflow do?
23.text: This Workflow will alert you, or a specified user, that a Todo has (or has not) been completed in a certain amount of time.You'll want to let the person know who is creating this Workflow the name of the Todo, the amount of time until the Todo must be completed, and what user(s) to notify. It's important to note that you can specify multiple users for the complete & incomplete Todo options. They can also be different people between both options.Let's start looking at notifications for Todo's that HAVE been created.Once the Workflows administrator sets up this example Workflow, you will receive both an in-app notification and a email notification once the specified Todo is completed.As you can see, this in-app notification shows that the Todo has been completed. The message shown after 'Workflow Alert' is customized by the administrator to say whatever you'd like.The email alert looks like this:Now, let's look at Todo's that have NOT been completed, or is inactive.The below shows what alert you will receive if the Todo is not completed by, or after the due date or delay time that you choose. The email alert looks similar:Whenever you click on any of these alerts, it will directly bring up the Todo window that is being referenced.

24.subject: Workflows for Users
24.topic: Workflow - Draw Status Updated & Multiple Outcomes
24.title: The Technical - What does this Workflow look like?
24.text: This Workflow is a bit complex looking - and that's because it is! Workflows are meant to take things that are both repetitive and complex and automate them for you. Let's take a look at this example. Say you want to create a Workflow trigger of 'Draw Status Updated', and set it to 'Rejected'. This means that this Workflow would start once a draw is rejected, within whatever projects you assign to it. In the below example, when a draw is rejected a specific user is alerted of that rejection. At the same time, a Todo is created and assigned to someone telling them they have 2 days to reach out to the rejecting party. There is then a 'Delay' question, which holds out for 2 days to see if the Todo is completed. After this, the 'Todo completed?' question will be asked. If yes, a user will be notified of this. If not, the original party will be notified of the inaction.

25.subject: Workflows for Users
25.topic: Workflow - Draw Status Updated & Multiple Outcomes
25.title: The Effect - What does this Workflow do?
25.text: When creating your starting trigger for this Workflow, it must be set to whatever draw status you'd like to trigger it. In this case, it's 'Rejected'.So, whenever a Draw is rejected (within the specified project(s)), this Workflow will start.The Trigger has started, and now there must be some sort of action. In this case, there are two. First off, a specific user or role will be notified that the draw has been rejected: Then, a Todo will be created and assigned to a specific party.You can set a due date for this, but we've already taken care of that by adding a delay before checking whether or not the Todo is completed. We've set the delay for this to 2 days, and then the Workflow will continue onto the next step: a question.What is the question? It is 'Todo Completed?' You can choose either a yes or no answer to this question, and then give consequences to each of those answers.In this case, both 'yes' and 'no' lead to an 'Alert User' action. One of them alerting a manager that the Todo hasn't been completed:And one that reaches out to another user to let them know it's been completed:Alerts and notifications are the same for these Workflow actions are the same as others: seen through in-app notifications and email notifications.

26.subject: Workflows for Users
26.title: The Technical - What does this Workflow look like?
26.text: This is a relatively simple Workflow. Whenever a file is linked, a Todo will be assigned and an alert will be sent to a user or role group.Instead of a user or group of users having to check and see if a file they need has been linked, they'll instead receive a notification. Click on over to the next step to see exactly what this Workflow will do!

27.subject: Workflows for Users
27.title: The Effect - What does this Workflow do?
27.text: As mentioned before, this is a relatively simple Workflow. The starting trigger would be 'File Linked'. As you can see below, you'll be notified whenever a file is linked to a custom field with the name you enter in. Once this trigger is activated, a user will be alerted per the setup in the Workflow. In this case, it's Casey Allman.Additionally, a Todo will be created and assigned to whoever you'd like. In this case, you may want to assign a Todo because you'd like to ensure a specific user will review the document within a specific period of time.

28.subject: Todos
28.title: Todos Overview
28.text: 1. What Are Todos?At their most basic concept, todos are simply a checklist of things "Todo," but they are so much more than that. Think of todos as a supercharged checklist, because that is exactly what they are. Todos let you visualize, organize and communicate about the work you have in front of you.Perhaps the greatest benefit to todos is their potential to centralize communication about the work you're doing, thereby reducing outgoing email. 2. Project TodosFrom within a project there are numerous tabs where you will find a "Todo" section. The exact locations where these "Todo" sections exist are elaborated on in section 2 of this training. But to generalize, from within a project, "Project Todos" are in locations locations such as "Updates, Dev, Marketing.. and more." The project "section specific Todo Lists" simply provide users with multiple Todo Lists to manage the different areas of work to be completed on a project. 3. Global TodosAs with the rest of DealforceCRE, there are "Global Todos" that administrators set for the rest of Dealforce. These are Todo lists that appear on whichever tab that is specified, throughout every project. In contrast, Project Todos are set within the project, within the specific tab, by any user of that project.4. Todo SubtasksWithin all types of todos, users have the ability to add subtasks. These are smaller, incremental parts of a todo that must be completed before a main todo can be marked off.

29.subject: Todos
29.title: Project Todos
29.text: 1. Project Todos OverviewThe tabs highlighted in red each have their own "Todos" section. Let's narrow in on one of these tabs and look at "Todos" more closely. 2. Todos & Todos ListsTo get started, click the button.Doing so will open the "Add Todo" window: Fill out all of the information starting from top to bottom Todo Title - should be a succinct name of the todoAssignee - person you're assigning the todo to (**NOTE: When assigning a user a todo they will receive an in-app notification) Followers - people receiving notificationsDue Date - date the todo is due File - allows the todo to be linked to a fileEmail - use this dropdown to link to an email listed on the Inbox tabDescription - a more detailed description of the todo Subtasks - it's possible to add smaller subtasks to a parent todo. These subtasks must be completed before the todo can be checked off.Notifications - these check boxes are all defaulted to be checked, as well as the value of 2 for days before the due date. Once done, clickAfter adding a few Todos, you have a Todos List. Additionally, when we hover over a "Todo," more features appear. New features that pop up on hover are outlined in red in the image below. Let's break down the various icons and features we have available to us here - The pencil icon allows you to edit the Todo after it's been created. - The info icon brings up the details of the Todo, including assignees, notification, and history of the Todo. You can also leave internal only and comments for all users to see. -The note icon will be greyed out if there is a description that has been added to the note, and will be see through if there isn't one. - The speech bubble brings up the same window as the info icon. The speech bubble is meant as a way to leave comments on the Todo. - The pointing finger button sends a reminder email to whoever the Todo is assigned to. The followers also get an alert. - The bell icon is struck out only if you're not set to be an assignee or follower for the todo. It's to signify whether or not you're set to be notified. - This buttons allows you to set a due date for the Todo. This can also be done during the creation, and by editing the Todo.3. SubtasksAs mentioned above, you can also add subtasks to a todo. If you do, it will look something like this once created:You cannot check off a todo that has subtasks until the subtasks have been completed. This is shown by a greyed out.To mark subtasks as completed, or to see what the subtasks are, simply click on the icon. The below screen will appear:As you can see, one subtask has been checked off, and one has not. To check one off, simply click on the box.

30.title: Global Todos View
30.text: DealforceCRE also offers a way to view various "Todos Lists" across all projects. This is done by clicking on the main "Todos" feature on the left hand-side of DealforceCRE. By default, the global Todo List will show only those Todos that are assigned to the user that is logged into the system. If you would like to see other Todos, you can click the 'x' next to your name in the Assignee filter field, or type additional names to view todos assigned to specific people.You can also enter additional filtering options such as searching by the name of the todo or by project.Clicking the Clear Filter link will revert the list back to the default which will show all todos in the system assigned to the current user.The results list can be sorted by either Project/SIR/Tenant or Due Date by clicking on the arrows next to the column header.New todos can be added from this screen as well by clicking the Add Todo button in the upper right of the screen. 35.subject: Schedule
35.title: Schedule Overview
35.text: Schedules allows users to view the various items within a project which must be executed in order to fully complete a project. 1. Schedule ItemsItems are broken down into three different types of schedule items, these items include: Tasks MilestonesCritical Paths2. Templates While re-creating similar schedule items for every single project would be repetitive, there are templates available for import. 3. Schedule ViewsSchedules offers multiple ways to visualize a project from beginning to end. From within a project, schedules can be viewed in: List ViewGantt View orCalendar View4. Global Schedule ViewAdditionally, from within the Schedules App, users can view schedule items from a global view. This global view is used to view all scheduled items for various projects in one summarized table.

36.subject: Schedule
36.title: Schedule Items (Tasks, Milestones, & Critical Paths)
36.text: 1. The building blocks of schedules A project Schedule is made up of different building blocks. The following list outlines those building blocks in order of smallest to largest. Tasks (The smallest parts of a schedule. The sum of all Tasks add up to a Milestone). Milestones(The sum of all Milestones add up to a Critical Path). Critical Paths (The sum of all critical paths add up to a project). 2. A demonstration on the Usage of Schedules First, we'll create a critical path, to which we will then create milestones to go within that critical path, followed by the creation of tasks to go within those milestones. To begin with schedules, first select a project. Once you have the proper project open, navigate to the "Schedule” tab. From here, you’ll see a blue button in the top right of the screen that looks like this:You can also Add a Schedule item from within the global view by clicking on the schedule app, and then clicking the button in the top right.When you click one of the above buttons, a new "Add Schedule Item" window in the foreground. First, choose the type of item you’re creating, for our purposes, we’ll choose "Critical Path." You’ll notice that by choosing “Critical Path,” the timeline section and duration section are hidden from the form. Key dates - These are global dates which are likely to occur on most projects. You will notice that if you check the key date box, the “Schedule Item Name” field disappears, and is instead replaced with a “Key Date Type” dropdown list of standardized Key Dates, which are useful for global reporting. You'll notice also that a few other checkboxes appear when check the "Key Date" checkbox: Legal ReqLocked? Remember to check these boxes if they pertain to your schedule item. Additionally, you will also get a tenant drop down field, here, choose the proper tenant for your schedule item. In many cases you will use the “Key Date” check box and one of the “Key Date Types” from the dropdown, but the system also allows users to create their own types of schedule items. To do this, simply make sure the “Key Date” checkbox is unchecked, and type in your item name. For this example, we’ll type in "Demo Critical Path 1". Next, if the form asks, choose a project the critical path will be associated with. There is also an option labeled "Blocking Schedule Items." This field is asking if there are any items which must be completed first before this item can be executed. Since this is our first item we’re adding to this project, there are no possible blocking items. Go ahead click the button in the bottom right of the window. This will take us to the "Notifications & Descriptions" area. From here, you can choose an Assignee & Followers. You may also choose how many days prior to a due date the Assignee is to be notified. The system defaults to check all notification boxes, but feel free to customize these. Next you can pick any tags you’d like to associate with this critical path. Finally, you can add a description. Once this is complete, go ahead and click the button at the bottom. Let’s now work on creating a few milestones, to demonstrate how it all fits together. From within the same project, click the button.Adding a milestone is mostly the same as adding a critical path, in that you have a Details section and a Notifications & Description section. However, the add Milestone window (as well as with the add Task window) has a few new fields and sections. One new field is the "Parent Schedule Item." The Parent Scheduled Item field allows you to designate to which parent item this new milestone belongs to. Since we’re creating a Milestone, the Parent Schedule Item would be the Critical Path we just created, "Demo Critical Path 1".Also, there are entire new sections such as the "Timeline" and "Duration" sections. For "Timeline", you’ll need to choose between Dependent and Independent. An independent timeline is one that is independent from any other items, therefore, you would designate both a start date and due date. A dependent timeline is a timeline whose start date and due date is dependent upon the due date of some other item. We’ll demonstrate using this option when we create a task in the next steps. For this first Milestone, we’ll choose an independent timeline with a specific start date and due date. The duration area auto populates the number of days until the item is due, however, you must specify if you would like the system to include weekends in that calculation. Remember to add any Notifications & Description settings you want and click “Save” when you’re done. We now have our first Milestone. Let’s now repeat this same process to create a second Milestone called, “Demo Milestone 2”, only here—we’ll give the item a Dependent timeline. In the example above, we made the timeline of Milestone 2 dependent upon the timeline of Milestone 1. We then specified that our new Milestone 2 is due 4 days after Milestone 1. We then saved the item for demonstration. Finally, let us create two tasks to show how it all fits together. This process looks identical to creating a milestone, with all the same options. The only difference is, we will select “Task” under the *Type dropdown. We have now created a Project Schedule!3. A (simple) but Complete Project ScheduleNavigate to the Project Schedule by going to the Projects app, typing in the name of the project, clicking the title of the project, and opening the schedule tab. From here you can get a view of project and its various scheduled items in what is known as “List View.” We see in the image below that there is one Critical Path with two Milestones. In Milestone 1, we have 2 tasks, and then within Milestone 2, there is 1 task. Note: the above example is overly simplified, an actual project schedule would include multiple Critical Paths with many more Milestones and Tasks within them. You can see by looking at the project’s list view, that the first milestone is due on September 30th, and the second milestone due October 4th, hence the Critical path due date of October 4th. A break down of the icons in this view. = An exclamation point is used to display a Critical Path. = A red exclamation point is used to display a Critical Path with a blocking scheduled item. = A target icon is used to display a Milestone = A solid circle with a number inside of it indicates a Milestone with nth number of tasks inside of it. = A red target indicates a Milestone or Task with a blocking scheduled item.= A solid red circle with a number inside of it indicates a Milestone with a blocking scheduled item and at least 1 task inside of it. = A triangle or ‘play’ icon indicates the schedule item is a task.Note: From this view, you can click on a parent item (critical path or milestone) to show or hide its child items. 4. Completing a Schedule ItemIn addition to some of the icons and status indicators covered just above, there are also a few ways to show the status of schedule items. You can see in the screen shot below, when I click on the (triangle) icon on a task, I get a few status options: Choosing the "In Progress" status will make that task, its parent milestone, and parent critical path all orange, since technically speaking, they would all be in progress at that point. **Note: you can only manually change the status of the tasks in the schedule. Milestones and Critical Paths inherit their status by their children items. In order to to make a Milestone turn blue (completed), you need to manually update the status of all tasks to "Completed." This is illustrated in the image below. Here - we see the "Project Kickoff" is now green (completed) because all of its tasks are marked blue. However, the Critical Path is still not Blue, because there are still are additional Milestones that are not complete.

37.subject: Schedule
37.title: Importing Templates
37.text: NOTE! Do not close the importer while the schedule template is importing. A Schedule TemplateA template with pre-built, commonly used schedule items. From within the schedule tab of a project, there is also a tool with a dropdown labeled “Actions.” Clicking on this gives you two options. One of which is Import Schedule Template. When clicking the “Import Schedule Template” button, a new "Schedule Customization" window will pop up. In the image below, in the top red box, users have the ability to choose which template they want to import by typing in a few characters of the project name that you are importing from. Here, we are choosing the New York, NY - Schedule Test. Also in the image below, in the bottom red box, we have a drop down to choose from either "All Critical Paths," or from "Individual Critical Paths."*Note: If you wish to include most critical paths, except for a few, it might make sense to import all critical paths, and then to delete those paths which you do not need. However, if you only need a few critical paths imported, it might make more sense to just import one path at a time. For this example, we will choose, "All Critical Paths." Next - choose a template start date, and finally, check whether to include the Assignees and Followers. Below is an overview of the imported template in List View. You will notice that all items import as inactive. To activate each item, hover over the name, click the edit icon and click Activate & Next.Clicking this button below switches to "Gannt View."*Note, we’ll be going over Gannt View in more detail in the next section. Here we can visualize the template we just imported. Please note that in this screenshot below, all of the items have been expanded. When initially navigating to Gannt View, all items will be collapsed.

38.subject: Schedule
38.title: Schedule Views (List View, Gannt View & Calendar View)
38.text: Now that we have created a basic schedule, let’s take a look at the various ways we can visualize the project. This can be done in three primary ways: List ViewGantt ViewCalendar View1. List ViewTo access the schedule items in a List View, click on the List View icon in the top right section: This is the view we used for a few of the prior sections in this Trainual. The schedule items are listed from top to bottom with a hierarchy tree. 2. Gannt Chart ViewTo access the schedule items in "Gannt Chart View," click on Gannt Chart icon in the top right section And you’ll see something like this: A "Gannt Chart" shows a series of horizontal bars which represent the amount of work done or production completed within a time period. In DealforceCRE, the items are displayed as such. Critical Paths - Are in GreenMilestones - Are in Pink Tasks - Are in BlueThese items are laid out on a grid that is broken up into different increments of time (days, weeks, months, years). We see a red vertical line in the image below. The line cuts through Thursday because that is when it was viewed. The length of the bar is as long as the amount of days there are to complete it. For instance, the bar for "Task 1" in the image below spans seven columns, or days, on the grid, because the task had a total of seven days to complete. Some of the bars also have yellow arrows pointing to other items, indicating to which items their timelines are dependent. From the image above, we can see that "Demo Milestone 1" has a yellow arrow pointing down to "Demo Milestone 2". This indicates that "Demo Milestone 2" has a dependent due date of 4 days after the completion of "Demo Milestone 1". Additionally, there are numerous options above the "Gannt Chart."The + and - magnifying glasses allow you to zoom in and out to view larger or shorter increments of time. The bracket squares allow you to change your Gannt view by either a weekly or monthly view.The filter button allows you to filter schedule items with the following filters:AssigneeDepartmentDate RangeBuyerTenantTags3. Calendar ViewThe "Calendar View" is perhaps the simplest schedule view. You access this view by clicking on the calendar icon in the top right section of the schedule view. This view allows users to view schedule items laid out on a monthly calendar. The main features above the calendar are: Search for an itemFilterActionsSwitch month One excellent feature of the "Calendar View" is that you can click on any green bar (or schedule item) within the calendar and the “Edit Schedule Item” window will pop up.

39.subject: Schedule
39.title: Global Schedule View
39.text: DealforceCRE also offers a way to view all projects side by side in a table. If you click on the 'Schedule' button on the left side bar the system will show the global schedule view. This is a list of projects with various filters to the right. 1. OrderingThe results shown in the "Global Schedule View" to the left can be re-ordered by clicking the name in the column header. For instance, clicking on "Schedule Item Name", will order results alphabetically by schedule item name. Clicking "Schedule Item Name" again will re-order the results from Z-A. *Note: If you order results in a certain way, then navigate away from the Schedule app, when returning, the set ordering will be saved. This is also true for the filters, which is explained in this section. 2. FiltersYou can also use filter section on the right hand side to filter results. Users can filter results by such criterion as: Project StateTypeAssigneeFollowersand MoreTo use filters, click a dropdown arrow on the right hand side, choose a value from the dropdown or type in a value you’re looking for. You can apply numerous filters, but as you do so, the specificity of the results of course increases. There are also a few check boxes throughout the filter section for filters such as: Key Dates OnlyInclude Past Dates Starred Projects onlyOnce all of the desired filters have been applied, click the "Apply" button at the bottom of filter section. The results will automatically re-populate to the left with your applied filters. To clear the filters, click on the clear filters button in this same location.From the main schedule view - you may also toggle between "List View, or Calendar View" to choose the global schedule items are being displayed. Last of all – there is a button to print the results in the condition that you have ordered and or filtered them.

45.subject: Inbox
45.title: Email Forwarding
45.text: This feature allows users to forward project relevant emails directly to the inbox tab of a project. Use case: A utility company sends an internal user an email about turning power on. This would be a perfect opportunity to forward the email directly to the project. That way, the email would be accessible to anyone working on the project. To accomplish this, the user would simply locate the corresponding project, and click on the inbox tab. From there, the user would locate the forwarding email and click on the clipboard icon. Now from within the user’s personal email, they can forward an email to the email address now copied to the clipboard. Once the user sends their email, the email will then appear in the inbox tab like so. There are then a few actions a user could take from within DealforceCRE regarding those emails. View - clicking on the (i) icon allows users to view the original email:From here, there are a number of different actions that can be taken: Viewing the emailAdding tags to the email A tagging system which allows users to type in their own custom tags, choose the name they’ve typed, and then filter emails by these tags. Example, you could tag an email regarding water, and an email regarding electricity as ‘Utilities,’ and then by choosing the ‘Utilities’ tag, users would only see those emails. Creating Todos / Schedule items from the actions button at the bottom.Detailed more in the next section:Users can also download the Project vCard using this button: Finally - users also have the ability to mass download vCards. This is done by clicking the 'actions' drop down from the global projects page. Users can simply filter the projects however they want, and then use the button to just download the vCards for that specific set of projects. Once the vCard file is downloaded to the users local computer, they can then import it using their preferred email system.

46.subject: Inbox
46.topic: Creating Todos / Schedule Items from an Email
46.title: Creating Todos / Schedule Items from an Email
46.text: In addition to the viewing the email, users can use the icons in the inbox index to create a todo, or a schedule item from an email.Clicking on the checkbox opens up the ‘Add Todo’ window. From here, the user would choose a ‘Todo List’ under the category dropdown. For utilities, one might choose the ‘Construction’ todo list as demonstrated in the image above. The user would then give the todo a title, enter in remaining details and click ‘save and close.’ When adding a todo at any time now, users now have an ‘email field.’ Clicking on the blue checkmark from the inbox index will cause this field to auto populate. This field also shows when adding a todo from any todo list as well. When adding a todo this way, the email dropdown will show all emails in the inbox as possible emails to associate to the todo. Clicking the blue calendar icon in the email index allows a user to create a schedule item from an email in the same exact manner as with creating Todos from emails.

47.subject: Notebook
47.title: Types of Notes
47.text: OverviewThe Notebook feature in DealforceCRE is located on the project 'Overview' tab, directly beneath the photo of the project. The Notebook panel includes tabs for inputting three different types of notes:Team NotesCEO NotesMy NotesDefault TabEach user can actually choose which tab is selected by default by going to their profile settings. Whichever tab is chosen in these settings will force that tab to open every time you land on the update tab or on meeting view. TabsThe Team Notes tab is for general notes that are directed at the whole team. Notes entered into this tab are visible by users with access to the project.CEO Notes is where management can post notes. These notes are also visible by users with access to the project.The My Notes tab works a little differently. Notes entered here can only be seen by the user that enters them.

48.subject: Notebook
48.title: Notes
48.text: Adding NotesAdding a note is the same for all tabs. First, go to the tab where you want to add the note and click on the blue 'Add Note' button.In the Add Note window, fill in the subject for the note and the details of the note. Options are also available to add tags and to notify other users. TagsIf tags are entered, they can be used to filter notes in the notebook. To add a tag, begin typing the word in the Tags box. If the tag exists, select it to add it to the field. If it does not yet exist, it will still appear in the list and clicking on it will add it to the field and make it available for use in future notes.A user might create a tag called 'Testing,' and when they do so, users could later on filter by this 'Testing' tag so that only notes with that tag are showing in the notebook. Notify UsersAny users added to the Notify field will receive a notification once the note is saved. **The Notify field is not available when entering notes in the My Notes tab since notes entered here are private.When all information has been entered, click Save.The note will now be listed within the corresponding tab on the project.Filtering by TagsAs mentioned earlier, the notebook can be filtered by the various tags used on notes. For instance, look at the image below, notice how there are two notes. One with a 'Financial' tag, as well as one with a 'Survey' tag. Let's say I only wanted to see the 'Financial' tags. I could accomplish this one of two ways. 1). Clicking on the actual tag shown to the right of a note would cause the notebook to filter and only show similarly tagged notes. (notice now that only 'development' notes are showing) 2). Users can also filter notes by clicking on the tag button in the bottom right of the notebook.

49.subject: Notebook
49.title: Editing Notes
49.text: Once a note has been added to either the Team Notes or CEO Notes tab, the name of the author will be listed next to it. These notes, however, can be edited by other users. If another user edits a note, their name will show there instead. The name shown will always be the person who most recently updated the note and the date/time will show when that was completed.To make an edit to a note, click the pencil icon next to the date/time for the note.In the Edit Note screen, make the necessary changes and click Save. An option to delete the note is also available on this screen, if needed.After saving, the Notebook will now show the updated text for the note as well as the user, date and time for the most recent change.

50.subject: Notebook
50.title: Meeting View
50.text: Editing and ViewingEditing and viewing existing notes in Meeting View is identical to the functionality of these areas on the Updates tab. The same notes tabs exist and clicking the pencil icon will bring up a window for editing the note.Adding NotesAdding a new note, however, is a bit different. Since notes may need to be entered at a faster pace while in Meeting View, fields are available for each tab to type notes into. These fields are located directly below the Notebook in the Meeting View window. It's at the lower left of the Meeting View screen. Upon posting the note, the notebook will actually automatically have the corresponding tab selected for viewing of the newly posted note. The Subject field for any notes added this way will be shown as Meeting View by default.

51.subject: Directory
51.title: Contacts
51.text: The Global Contacts list is nested within Directory > Contacts, found in the Global Menu on the left. New contacts can be added by clicking thebutton in the upper right. In the Add Contact window, the only required field is the Contact Name. However, all available information should be entered and an email address is required in order to give the contact access to DealforceCRE as an external user. When all information has been entered, click Save.The new contact should now appear in the list.Once the contact is in the list, there are a few options available.Clicking on the Contact Name will bring up a profile summary for that contact. From this screen, the contact information can be edited by clicking the Edit Contact button in the upper right. You can set assigned Projects, Permissions, and also see Activity if you're an Admin.If you are granting access to a contact and making them an external user, they must have a company chosen on their contact details, as well as an email address. Clicking the Company Name will take the user to a similar profile summary screen for the company.Clicking on the Email Address will open a new email from your default email client addressed to that email.At the far right, icons are available to edit or delete the contact. Note: If the contact is linked to any bids, payments, etc., the system will not allow them to be deleted.There is a search bar at the top to help find a specific contact. Also, the majority of the columns are sortable and a Contact Type filter is available.Takeaway: Once you add a contact, you can associate them to a company in the directory. You can also grant these contacts access to your application.

52.subject: Directory
52.title: Companies
52.text: The Global Companies list is nested within Directory > Companies, found in the Global Menu on the left.The Companies screen works very similarly to the Contacts screen. To add a new company, click the Add Company button in the upper right.As with Contacts, only the Company Name is required, but it is encouraged that all available information be entered prior to saving.After saving, the new company will appear in the list.Clicking on the Company Name will bring up the Company Profile Summary page. Edit and Delete buttons are also available at the right side.On the Company Profile Summary page, company notes can be added and relevant files can be uploaded. New contacts can also be added and linked to the company by clicking 'Contacts', and then clicking 'Add Contact' button.Specific companies can be found by using the search bar at the top of the company list. There is also a Company Type filter and most columns are sortable.Take away: Once companies are added here in the directory, they can be associated to contacts using the 'Company' field on the edit contact window.

54.subject: Directory
54.title: Entities
54.text: The Global Entities list is nested within Directory > Entities, found in the Global Menu on the left. Click 'Add Entity' to add a new Entity.In the Add Entity screen, the Entity Name and Status are both required fields. The Status defaults to Unavailable, but can be changed at any time.After saving, the new entity will show in the list. Clicking the Entity Name will bring up the Entity Detail screen. Entities can also be edited or deleted by clicking on the corresponding icons.In order to assign an Entity to a Project, click the Edit icon that appears when you hover your cursor over the entity. Type the project name or location into the Projects field and select the project. Note: You can assign only one project to an Entity, and one Entity to a project. If you attempt to link 2, you'll have to include a justification for multiple projects (Split Parcel, or Rule 1031).After linking a project, the Status will now show Assigned and the chosen Project will appear below the status.A specific entity can be searched for in the Search bar. This screen also has options for filtering by status and all columns are sortable. There is also a Download button available that will export a .csv file with all of the entity information.Once assigned to a project, an entity can be either viewed, or edited, from a project if the user has permissions to entities. The entity will appear beneath the project title, as shown below:

55.subject: Directory
55.title: Entities - File Management
55.text: Some of the functions of the entities modal are self explanatory, like the entity name, EIN, status, projects, etc. However there are some file functions that are unique to the entities modal that could use some more explanation: Attached Files W9 - This refers to the ability to upload a W9 for an entity. To do this, just drag and drop the file onto the red button beneath the header, or click to attach the file.Attached Project Files - This file area allows you to choose files that are already a part of a project, and attach them to the entity. You can choose from the project(s) that are attached to the entity. The app allows you to search through the project folder tree for the needed file.Attached Global Files - This file area allows for file linking from the "Entities" folder, that is within every instance folder tree. Simply drag and drop any local file to this folder, and attach them from the "Attached Global Files" area.

56.subject: Directory
56.title: Tenants
56.text: Adding tenants is within the Companies directory because technically all tenants are Companies.Tenants can be added by going to Directory > Companies from the Global Menu on the left. From here, you'll want to select the company that you want to add a tenant to. You'll do that by searching for the specific company, and then selecting it's name.Once you pull up the company page, you'll want to click on the 'View Trade Name' button near the top right of the screen.The next screen looks similar, except now there's a button that says 'Add Company'. Click that.The below screen comes up, allowing you to add all needed details for the tenant. The most important step here is to ensure you check the 'Tenant' box next to the company name. You will also want to ensure you have the correct 'Company Trade Name' selected. This is the company that the tenant is part of. Fill out all needed fields and press save at the bottom of the pop-up.Once you complete these steps, you'll be taken back to the main Company Trade Name screen with a list of companies associated and their status as tenants.Clicking the Tenant Name will bring up the Tenant/Company Profile Summary screen. Clicking the 'View Trade Name' button will allow you to see what company the selected company is a tenant of, or if that company has tenants or other companies (such as vendors) assigned to it.

57.subject: Custom Fields
57.title: Custom Fields - What are they?
57.text: Custom fields are a great place to house important fields for each DealforceCRE tab. For example, you may have fields that you need only for specific projects, and only within the Finance tab. You can house these custom fields here. They are called 'custom fields' because not only can you name them whatever you'd like, but you can assign a specific field type that corresponds with your need. The fields you can assign are:Short TextLong TextDateDollarsLink to ChecklistPercentageContact/Company SelectionFeetSquare FeetYes/NoLink to FileLink to FolderLink to Key DateTodo ListLinked FieldPhoto SelectionYou can assign custom fields in almost every tab. To find them, click the tab you'd like to create custom fields on, scroll down to near the bottom of the page on the left.

58.subject: Custom Fields
58.title: Custom Fields - Adding a Custom Field
58.text: To add a custom field to a tab, navigate to the 'custom fields' area of whichever tab you'd like to add custom fields to. Click the 'Add Custom Field' button.Once you do this, the below modal appears:From here, you'll choose what you'd like to name your custom field, and what field type you'd like it to be. As mentioned in the previous section, these are all of the field types available to you:Short TextLong TextDateDollarsLink to ChecklistPercentageContact/Company SelectionProject Role SelectionFeetSquare FeetYes/NoLink to FileLink to FolderLink to Key DateTodo ListLinked FieldPhoto SelectionLink to URL

59.subject: Custom Fields
59.title: Custom Fields - Using & Deleting
59.text: To use a custom field, click on the 'edit' text to the right of the custom field name:Fill in whatever the field requires, per what field type you chose in the previous creation step. In this example, the 'date' custom field was selected. Once you're finished, click the to save your changes, or click the to cancel and not save changes.To delete a custom field, you'd click the icon within the edit menu of the custom field. Note: You cannot delete custom fields that have been globally implemented. That is an administrative tool.

61.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
61.title: An Introduction
61.text: Construction Contracts are a type of contract that can be entered in DealforceCRE. These contracts are entered by going to the Budget tab, and clicking on Construction Contracts. The power of the Construction Contracts is that they can be linked to a bid, as well as linked to budget tasks. When contingency is set on a budget, that contingency can then be monitored when subsequent change orders are received. Once these contracts are created, construction change orders can be added to the contract.

62.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
62.title: Adding a Construction Contract
62.text: Contract DetailsIn order to create a Construction Contract, you first need to make sure you have the correct permissions for it. On the Permissions tab within the Edit User screen, select either Read Only or Read/Write under Budget Contracts.The first step is to go to the Budget tab and select Construction Contracts.Select the Add Construction Contract button. First, choose an Internal Point of Contact. Next, select the Payee. If they do not exist in the list, add them by clicking on the +New Contact button.The Notice Address information will auto-populate based on the address on file for your company.Enter a Contract Name and Contract Amount. While not required, the optional fields of Linked Bid, Commencement Date, Budget Tasks and Notes are also available. When all information has been entered, click Next.Pay App DefaultsOn the Pay App Defaults tab, it's important to set information that will be used in any future pay application which the construction contract is tied to. You can sit distribution and retainage, required documents, and who the approvers, signers, and document verifiers are. Finally, you can also add followers to this area that will automatically become followers for any pay app this contract is tied to.Change Order DefaultsOn the Change Order Defaults tab, enter the ‘standard’ options for change orders entered against this contract. These details can be changed on a case by case basis when entering a change order if it does not follow the typical settings. This will save time when adding change orders.Enter the Project Number, Phone, and Fax, if available.There are a few alternative methods for entering the General Conditions, Profit, and Gross Receipts/Sales Tax percentages. Checking the first box under these fields will remove the Profit field and combine it with the General Conditions field. The second box will remove the Gross Receipts/Sales Tax field and require manual entry of this percentage when the change order is entered.Next, a default Approver needs to be chosen for submitted change orders. This can be any internal or external user in DealforceCRE.Last, select a default signer for change orders. As with requesting signature on other files in DealforceCRE, multiple signers can be chosen and a signing order can be set. When complete, click Save.Once the contract has been saved, it will show in the list under Construction Contracts. The contract can be edited by clicking the pencil icon. If a bid has been linked to the contract, clicking on the bid name will bring you to the Bid Package Details screen.Now that a contract is in place, change orders can be applied against it.

64.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
64.title: Adding a Change Order
64.text: PermissionsOnce a Construction Contract has been created in the system, users can then create Construction Change Orders. First off, in order to be able to create a Construction Change Order you must have the proper permissions. In the permissions section of the edit user window, there’s now a new line item called: Budget Change OrdersIn addition, users also need the ability to at least 'Read Only' on Budget Contracts.And finally, users also need to have read/write permissions for approval requests. Users must have read/write access in order to be able to actually create these change orders. Also, in order to create a change order, there must be at least one existing construction contract on a project. Once a contract is in the system, and you’re ready to create a change order, click on the budget tab dropdown menu and choose the ‘Construction Change Orders’ option. Doing so will take users to the Construction Change Orders Page.Change Order Tab LayoutLet’s break down all the sections before we begin creating Change Orders. First off, next to the header ‘Construction Change Orders,’ users will always see the ‘Total Hard Cost Contingency Remaining.’ Then there is a change order search bar, where users can search by company, submitter or contractor name. Users can also search by statuses such as: draft, submitted, partially approved, approved, partially executed, fully executed, rejected or voided. Add Construction Change OrderTo get started adding a construction change order, click on the blue ‘Add Construction Change Order’ button in the top right. Doing so will open the ‘Add Construction Change Order’ window. To start, you simply need to choose a contract to which this change order exists. Once you choose a contract, the remaining fields of the ‘Add Construction Change Order’ will appear. All of the values for each field should be automatically populated based upon the Change Order defaults that were set during the creation of the construction contract this Change Order is related to. If any settings need to be changed, users may adjust these settings at this time. Finally, users may also upload one support document to this change order. As noted here on the upload button, additional documents can be uploaded at a later time if needed. The document is not required at this time, but if there is a supporting document, it can be uploaded now.

65.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
65.title: Change Order Index
65.text: When users create at least one Change Order, they will see these Change Orders in the Change Order index on this page. By default, the change order’s status will default to ‘draft.’ In addition to statuses, the Change Order index also shows the Change Order Number (number in which it was entered), the company, the user who submitted the Change Order, the number of line items, the Contract name, Reimbursable Status, and Refundable Status. From here, users can click the 'Actions' button near the top right of the screen and choose 'Edit' to edit the Change Order

66.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
66.title: Change Order Overview
66.text: Change Order DetailsFirst - You have the Change Order Details section. This section shows general details in the top. In addition the Change Order Details, internal users also have a Budget Hard Cost Contingencies section. This section shows the Hard Cost total that was entered on the budget. Also - this section shows how much Hard Cost contingency is left in the budget. This is here for internal users to track total hard costs that were budgeted for, as well as monitor how much contingency remains, information that is vital when approving Change orders. There is also a Contract Change Orders Section - this shows total executed, total unexecuted, total Submitted, and finally there is total Change Order drafts. Also in this Change Order Details section, you have a comment box. Here, comments can be left by both internal and external parties with access to the Change Order overview.Supporting DocumentsAt the bottom right you have the document preview section, which is seen in the image below. Using the dropdown in the blue box, users can change which attachment they are viewing. Users can upload additional documents using the 'upload supporting documents' button to the right, or they can download the chosen document using the 'download' button to the right of that. Then you also have the Line Item sections. This area will be detailed in the next section of this training module.

67.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
67.title: Line Items (& Submitting Change Orders)
67.text: Change Order Line ItemsAn important part of the Change Order Overview screen is the Line Items section. This is where the individual line items will appear as they are entered by the internal users. The example below has a few line items listed out. The totals are in the bottom right. To start, click on the ‘Add Line Item’ button. This will open up the ‘Add Line Item’ window. From here you must enter in all fields: Enter a description, the company doing the work, the commencement date and then the Item cost and quantity. For item cost, you enter the cost per unit. Such as $25.00 For Quantity, you enter how many of the item is there are. Example, choosing 4 would be a total (before taxes, profits and overhead) of $100.00.
