In the example from earlier, we set up the Taxes, profits and overhead to be 15%. Therefore, this line item’s total after taxes profit and overhead would be $115. When finished with each line item, click ‘add line item.’ So long as the change order hasn’t been submitted yet, the details for the separate line items are editable. In addition to being able to edit these line items, users can also comment on the individual line items. To do so, simply click the icon.Doing so will open the ‘Change Order Line Item Details’ window. From here, you have an information section, a history section and also a comments section. All the line items will total in the totals section along with any added profit and overhead, as well as Gross receipts / sales taxes. Submitting the Change OrderOnce all items have been added, and all entered information has been verified, the Internal user would click the 'Submit Change Order' button.Once this occurs, the change order will change from a Draft status, to a Submitted status. Once the change order has been submitted, notifications will be sent to the designated approvers to verify.

68.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
68.title: The Approval Process
68.text: **Note** When an approving order is set, the approval requests go out one at a time, waiting for each person to respond before subsequent approval requests are sent out. If one user rejects the Change Order, it becomes fully rejected and the Change Order approval request gets returned to the original user who submitted the Change Order. The following example is for when there is an approving order set. Once the Change Order has been submitted, the first approver would receive an approval request. If the change order is rejected by the owner, the change order would go back to the user who initially entered it and they would need to make any necessary adjustments prior to resubmitting for approval.Now, when the first approver approves the change order, this “approved” will show in the change order history on the change order overview screen. The next approver would then receive an approval request. Once approved by this second and final party, the signature process begins.

69.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
69.title: The Signing Process
69.text: Once approved by all parties, a few events occur: 1). A physical Change Order document is created. 2). The Change Order is saved in the documents section of the Change Order overview. As well as in the Construction Change Orders folder. 3). That physical Change Order is then sent to the owner at the same time for signature from both parties. Both the internal user (owner) and the external user (requestor) will receive an email that looks like the following. Signature ProcessWhen the signers click the ‘Review and Sign’ button they will be taken to the file overview screen, with the ability to DocuSign the change order. The signers would check the box to agree to the DocuSign terms, and click the yellow continue button. From here the signers would follow the traditional DocuSign prompts of adopting a signature, signing the documents, and clicking the finish button. Once finished, both internal and external parties will receive a notification stating that the signatures have been completed on the change order. For both internal and external users, the change order will now have a status as ‘fully executed’ in the Change Order Index. Changing signer for a Construction Change OrderThere may be a time when the signer for a change order is not available to sign, and it has to be changed to a different signer. To do this, you change the signer to a one time signer. To change the signer to a one time signer: Navigate to the "Change Order History" section.Click "Edit Signers"Navigate to the "Change Order Defaults" tab.Scroll down to the "Signature Process" section and click "Set One-Time Signature Process"5. Set who you want to be the one-time signer for this construction change order.6. Click save. 7. Click "Resend Request" in the "Change Order History" section of the change order.

70.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
70.title: Viewing and Downloading Fully Executed Change Orders
70.text: Viewing the Signed Change Order**note - as each new change order is added to a project, a new enumerated folder is added to the ‘Construction Change Orders’ folder like such: Then when all parties approve a Change Order, the new Change Order that is generated will get saved in the correct ‘Construction Change Order’ folder. If we were on change order 3 right now, these newly created change orders would appear in the folder titled 3.Users can also access these Change Orders from the Change Order overview screen. From here, using the files section, users can use the drop down to choose the newly signed Change Order (it will be the file with a number followed by an X).Downloading the Change OrderTo download the signed Change Order, simply choose that file from the dropdown, and click the download button in the top right. The pdf will download to the user’s local computer.

71.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
71.topic: Construction Change Orders for External Users
71.title: Granting Permissions
71.text: To add a Construction Change Order, the external user would simply click the 'Add Construction Change Order' button.

72.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
72.topic: Construction Change Orders for External Users
72.title: Entering a Change Order
72.text: To get started adding a Change Order, external users would click the blue 'Add Construction Change Order' button in the top right of the screen. When they do so, the 'Add Construction Change Order' window will pop up. At this point there will only be one field - 'Contract'From here, the external user would choose the construction contract to which this Change Order will exist. As soon as a contract is chosen, the remaining fields will appear. The values for these fields are then populated automatically from the Change Order defaults that the internal party set when creating the construction contract. The default values that pull in should all be accurate, and no further action should be required from the external user to adjust these values. If anything looks off, these fields can be adjusted now.The external party would then scroll to the bottom of the window, upload one supporting document (more documents can be uploaded in the next step), and finally, they would click save, which creates the Change Order.

73.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
73.topic: Construction Change Orders for External Users
73.title: Viewing Change Orders as an External Users
73.text: Change Order StatusesNewly created change orders will have a status of 'Draft.' This means that the Change Order is still being drafted, and that it has not been submitted for approval. Once a user clicks this red info icon (to the right of a change order), the user is taken to the Change Order Overview Screen.Change Order OverviewFirst - You have the Change Order Details section. This section shows general details in the top, as well as total executed (fully approved and signed change orders), total unexecuted (total of change order amounts submitted by unsigned), total Submitted (this is all change orders, both signed and unsigned, that have been submitted), and finally there is total drafts (entered line items on change orders that haven't been submitted yet). Also there is a 'Change Orders Comments' section where external users can communicate directly with the internal party by simply typing in a comment and clicking 'send'.At the bottom right you have the document preview section, which is seen in the image below. Using the dropdown in the red box, the user can change which attachment they are viewing. Users can upload additional documents using the 'upload supporting documents' button to the right, or they can download the chosen document using the 'download' button to the right of that. Then you also have the Line Item sections. This is where the individual line items will appear as they are entered by the internal users. The example below has a few line items listed out. The totals are in the bottom right. Adding Line Items will be detailed in the next step of this module.

74.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
74.topic: Construction Change Orders for External Users
74.title: Adding Line Items and Submitting the Change Order
74.text: To get started, click the blue 'Add Line Item' button in the top right.The 'Add Line Item' window will appear.All of the following fields here are required. Enter a description, the company doing the work, the commencement date and then the Item cost and quantity. For item cost, you enter the cost per unit. Such as $25.00 For Quantity, you enter how many of the item there are. Example, choosing 4 would be a total (before taxes, profits and overhead) of $100.00. In the example from earlier, we set up the Taxes, profits and overhead to be 15%. Therefore, this line item’s total after taxes profit and overhead would be $115. When finished with each line item, click ‘add line item.’ So long as the change order hasn’t been submitted yet, the details for the separate line items are editable. In addition to being able to edit these line items, users can also comment on the individual line items. To do so, simply click the icon.Doing so will open the ‘Change Order Line Item Details’ window. From here, you have an information section, a history section and also a comments section.All the line items will total in the totals section along with any added profit and overhead, as well as gross receipts / sales taxes.Submitting the Change OrderOnce all items have been added, click the 'Submit Change Order' button. Once this occurs, the change order will change from a 'draft' status, to a ‘submitted’ status. Once the change order has been submitted, notifications will be sent to the designated approvers to verify.

75.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
75.topic: Construction Change Orders for External Users
75.title: Approving Change Orders
75.text: Approval ProcessIf there is an approving order, the approvals will go out one at a time. At this time, the external user would receive an in-app notification, as well as an email notification, stating that their approval has been requested on a Change Order.When it is the external users turn to approve the document, they simply approve or reject using these buttons. If the external user is rejecting the document, they should leave some general comments in the bottom left comment section of the Change Order Overview section, or on a line item itself, as to why they are rejecting the Change Order. If rejected, by any party, the Change Order will not move on to the next step, the signature process.Once the external user is ready to approve the document, they can simply click 'approve.' The Change Order will move into the 'Approved' status.Once all approvals occur, a Change Order is generated into a PDF format, and is sent to both the requestor (external user) and the owner (internal party) to sign via DocuSign.

76.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
76.topic: Construction Change Orders for External Users
76.title: Signing Change Orders
76.text: Change Order CreationOnce approved by all parties, a few events occur: 1). A physical Change Order document is created. 2). The Change Order is saved in the documents section of the Change Order overview. 3). That physical Change Order is then sent to the owner at the same time for signature from both parties. The external user (the requestor) will receive an email that looks like the following. Signature ProcessWhen the external user (requestor) hits the ‘Review and Sign’ button they will be taken to the file overview screen, with the ability to DocuSign the change order. The external user (requestor) would check the box to agree to the DocuSign terms, and click the yellow continue button. From here the external user (requestor) would follow the traditional DocuSign prompts of adopting a signature, signing the documents, and clicking the finish button.Once finished, both internal and external parties will receive a notification stating that the signatures have been completed on the change order. For both internal and external users, the change order will now have a status as ‘fully executed’ in the Change Order Index.

77.subject: Construction Contracts & Change Orders
77.topic: Construction Change Orders for External Users
77.title: Viewing / Downloading Fully Executed Change Orders
77.text: Viewing the Signed Change OrderTo view the signed change order, users can click on the red "i" info icon, which appears when hovering over the change order in the index.From here, using the files section, external users can use the drop down to choose the newly signed Change Order (it will be the file with a number followed by an X).Downloading the Change OrderTo download the signed Change Order, simply chose that file from the dropdown, and click the download button in the top right. The pdf will download to the user’s local computer.

78.subject: Construction RFI's
78.title: RFI Permissions
78.text: Construction RFI’s internal users should have the following permissions. When external users are added on to an RFI package, they will automatically gain the proper permissions they need to use RFI’s.Once the permission has been set for an internal user, they can then navigate to a project to begin using this feature.

79.subject: Construction RFI's
79.title: RFI User Types
79.text: The whole point of these construction RFI’s is to allow a place for the commercial real estate developer, general contractor, architect, or any other external party to assign RFI’s to each other. Once these RFI’s are created, they are a place for communicating, collaborating on and completing RFI’s. RFI Packages require RFI Users Types in order to work. RFI User Types are simply a list of user types to be used on RFI’s. External parties such as General Contractors, Architects, or Engineers would be considered RFI User Types. Think of these as the types of users you’d like to interact with you on RFI’s. To add RFI User Types, go to (Your Name) > List and Tools > Categories/Lists > RFI & Submittal User Types. From here, click the 'Add RFI & Submittal User Type' button in the top right to add your user types. Once these user types are added you can proceed to the next step.

80.subject: Construction RFI's
80.title: Creating an RFI Package
80.text: To get started with Construction RFI’s, an internal user should navigate to a project. Once there, they can locate the construction tab. Click on this and a dropdown menu should appear. From here, click the “New RFI Package” option. Once this button is clicked, the “Add RFI Package” window will open. To start filling out this window, enter in an RFI package name, and followers. Followers are internal users that should receive updates about construction RFI’s. Next, you’ll want to set the user types for this RFI, as well as associate these user types to actual external users. The RFI User Types list defined in the previous step are now accessible on this form. Clicking the “User Type” dropdown field, you’ll see the list created. For each user type selected, an associated user should be chosen from the user field to the right. If additional user types are needed, simply click the “+Add User” button. Your user type settings should look something like this when complete. Once all these RFI Package settings are entered, you can click “save” and the RFI package will be created. Please note, that any external users associated with a user type will automatically be given the permissions they need to access the RFI package. When the RFI package is created there will be a link for the new RFI package under the construction tab. Clicking this will open up the RFI Package. In the middle of the RFI Package you'll see 'Edit RFI Details', which will allow you to edit the settings you just chose.

81.subject: Construction RFI's
81.title: Creating New RFI's
81.text: Below the RFI details is the RFI Index, at this point, there wouldn’t be any RFI’s in this index. To add a new RFI, click the button to the right. Doing so will open the “New RFI” window. You can think of these RFI’s sort of like todos. In that they have an assignee, followers, a due date, and details. RFI’s have a few other fields as well. The first field is “Requestor”, this field is only seen by the internal team when creating a new RFI. In other words, the internal team can create a new RFI on behalf of the CRE Development company, or even on behalf of the other user types on the RFI package. In the example below, the CRE developer is creating an RFI on behalf of the company, assigning it to the General Contractor, and making the Architect a follower, which will mean the architect will also be able to view and interact with the RFI. Next, you’ll want to set a date issued and a date response is due (due date). By default, the new RFI will have a status of new, this can be left this way in most cases. Now enter a subject, information, and attach any files if needed. Once completed, click the “save” button. You’ll see the new RFI in the RFI index.

82.subject: Construction RFI's
82.title: RFI Index
82.text: The RFI index shows all RFI’s and all important details. In the example given, we assigned the RFI to the General Contractor, once the RFI was created, the General Contractor would have received a notification stating that they are assigned this RFI. The Architect would have also received a notification since they were added as a follower on this RFI as well. Please note that internal users can view all created RFI’s, however, external users can only view RFI’s which they are a requestor, assignee, or follower on. That means that a General Contractor can assign an RFI to the Architect, but if there was an Engineer on the RFI package as well, and wasn’t specifically added as a follower on the RFI, the Engineer would NOT see the RFI in the RFI index.

83.subject: Construction RFI's
83.title: Interacting with RFI's
83.text: Near the status column in the RFI index, there are three icons that allow for different actions. The finger icon allows users to send a nudge or a reminder to the RFI assignee. The pencil opens up the “Edit RFI” window.The eye icon opens the RFI Details and Response window. This is the window that assignees, followers, and requestors go to update or complete RFI’s.

84.subject: Construction RFI's
84.title: RFI Responses
84.text: The RFI Details and Responses window is where a user would post a response or close an RFI. The top portion of this window has general details about the RFI, as well as a place for uploading and viewing attached files. The status field below is where a user would set an RFI to new, in progress, closed, or rejected. Below this field is the RFI responses section. Here users can post new responses, and view other RFI responses. A posted response should look something like this: All followers on an RFI will receive notifications about each of these responses. When an assignee is ready to post their final response, they should simply click the ‘Final Response?’ checkbox before posting their comment.

85.subject: Construction RFI's
85.title: Closing RFI's
85.text: And when the RFI is completed, the assignee should change the RFI status to “Closed”. In the example below the user has posted a final response, and closed the RFI. They would simply click “save” at this point to finish the RFI. The status will then show as “Closed”, all followers will receive a notification that the RFI has been closed, and notifications relative to the “Date Response Required” will cease. Of course if the RFI is not completed by the Date Response Required, then notifications explaining this will be sent out to followers.And that’s it for Construction RFI’s.

86.subject: Construction RFI's
86.title: Opening Construction RFI's
86.text: To get started with creating, or responding to an RFI, head to the desired project, and click on the construction tab. A dropdown menu will appear. Here, you should see the name of a construction RFI package.Click on this to be taken to the RFI package.

87.subject: Construction RFI's
87.title: Creating New RFI's
87.text: Once you land on the RFI package, you should see a page with two primary sections, you have the details at the top, and then below the RFI details is the RFI Index. You can think of RFI's as tasks that you can assign to other parties, or tasks that other parties (or the developer) are assigning to you. RFI's have an assignee, followers, a due date, and details.To add a new RFI, click the “New RFI” button to the right. Doing so will open the “New RFI” window.First off, you can choose an assignee type. If the chosen type is assigned to a user within the RFI, they will automatically be set as the assignee. This does not prevent you from changing the assignee if needed. An assignee can be added manually, this is the developer or third party that is responsible for completing your RFI. Followers can be added as well. Followers should be used when there is some other third party that should be privy to the RFI details. By default, the new RFI will have a status of new, this can be left this way in most cases. If you check the "Urgent" checkbox, the assignee will be notified that an urgent RFI has been created. Now enter a subject, information, and attach any files if needed. Once completed, click the “save” button. You’ll see the new RFI in the RFI index. At this point, please note that the assignee, followers, and development team will receive email notifications informing them a new RFI has been submitted. Alternatively, one of the other third parties on the project might follow these same steps and assign an RFI to you, to which you would receive an email notification.

88.subject: Construction RFI's
88.title: RFI Index
88.text: The RFI index shows all RFI’s and all important details. From this index, you can see any RFI's you've assigned to others, RFI's you're a follower on, as well as view any RFI's that are assigned to you.

89.subject: Construction RFI's
89.title: Interacting with RFI's
89.text: Near the status column in the RFI index, there are between 1 to 3 icons that are there depending on the status of the RFI.The finger icon allows users to send a nudge or a reminder to the RFI assignee. The pencil opens up the “Edit RFI” window. You will only see the pencil icon if you created the RFI. The eye icon opens the RFI Details and Response window. This is the window that assignees, followers, and requestors go to to respond to or complete RFI’s.

90.subject: Construction RFI's
90.title: RFI Responses
90.text: The RFI Details and Responses window is where a user would post a response or close an RFI. The top portion of this window has general details about the RFI, as well as a place for uploading and viewing files. The status field below is where a user would change an RFI from new, to in-progress or closed. Below this field is the RFI responses section. Here, users can post new responses, and view other RFI responses. A posted response should look something like this: All followers on an RFI will receive notifications about each of these responses. When an assignee is ready to post their final response, they should simply click the ‘Final Response?’ checkbox before posting their comment.

91.subject: Construction RFI's
91.title: Closing RFI's
91.text: When the RFI is completed, the assignee should change the RFI status to “Closed”. In the example below the user has posted a final response, and closed the RFI. They would simply click “save” at this point to finish the RFI. The status will then show as “Closed”, all followers will receive a notification that the RFI has been closed, and notifications relative to the “Date Response Required” will cease. If the RFI is not completed by the Date Response Required, then a notification explaining this will be sent out to followers.And that’s it for Construction RFI’s.

92.subject: Bid Management
92.title: Creating A New Bid Package
92.text: 1. Navigate to a project and click the Bids tab. It may also be in the 'All Tabs' drop down. You should see the option to create a New Bid Package. Click that.2. Fill out the Bid Package DetailsBid Package Name: A generic name visible to internal and external users.Bid Package Status: New, Pre-Bid, Out for Bid, Awarded. These must be manually set.Project SqFt: The total square footage for the bid.Building SqFt: The total square footage for the building. This is not required if you prefer to include it in the "Project SqFt" field.Land SqFt: The total square footage for the land. This is not required if you prefer to include it in the "Project SqFt" field.Bid Package Contact: The internal or external user that's responsible for the bid package.Followers: Internal or external users that should be apprised of updates to the bid package.Bid Package Due Date and Time.Anticipated Award Date.Set a reminder frequency for bidders and followers.3. Connect a bid folder to a bid. You cannot attach an empty folder to a bid, so first you will need to go to the Files tab. Locate the folder for your bid under Construction > Bid Packages. Once you have added the pertinent files, then you can go back to the bid to connect your folder.To do this, click Connect Folder and select the existing folder from the Files section in that project. You'll only be searching for folders within that project, and you can change the selected folder at any time.4. Select a Bid Template to use. There are pre-made templates that can be selected on the left, or you can create or edit an existing template.To save a new template, just enter the name on the top right where it says Enter New Template NameYour bid package is now ready to be shared with bidders.

93.subject: Bid Management
93.title: Inviting Bidders
93.text: Bidders must be invited to a bid package in order to provide a bid. If you cannot find the external user you are looking for, they may not yet have an account. To add a new external user, visit the Contacts page in the project and then click Add New External User.1. To invite a new bidder, click the 'Add Bidder' button on the right side of the Bid screen, and select 'Invite Bidder' from the drop down.2. Select who you would like to invite by typing out the name and then selecting the external user. You can select multiple people to receive the email invitation. The emails will be delivered separately, so they will not know who else is bidding.Anyone you select that has not been given access to the project already will be given access to the project.The external user will receive an email requesting their bid.3. Bidders will then need to accept or decline their bid invitation.

94.subject: Bid Management
94.title: Bid Package Notifications
94.text: The following notifications will be delivered throughout the bidding process:Whenever a comment is left on the bid overview page, the external user or bid contact will receive a notification.When a bid invitation is responded to by an external user.When an RFI response is submitted.When a bidder is awarded.When a bid update is received.When an RFI is submitted.When a bid sheet has been submitted.When the current user is added as a bid package follower.You can adjust the notification preferences by clicking your name in the top right and scrolling to the bid section.

95.subject: Bid Management
95.title: Accepting a Bid Invitation
95.text: When you are invited to bid on a new bid package, you'll be asked to accept or decline the bid invitation. To do so, follow these steps.1. You should have received an email inviting you to a new bid. Go ahead and click that button.If you're an existing user, you can also log into DealforceCRE and visit the bids page by finding the appropriate project. If not, you will need to register first.2. Once you've found the correct project or have clicked the button in the invitation email, you will see a notification at the top of the screen asking if you would like to accept or decline the invitation. This lets the internal staff know of your intention, and your answer can be changed at any time.3. After you make your selection, the internal staff will be notified. If you've accepted, you may begin filling out the bid sheet at this time.4. If your intention to bid changes at any time, you can click Actions and then Decline or Accept Invitation. You can also choose to send out invites to other Collaborators in your company.

96.subject: Bid Management
96.title: Filling out a Bid Sheet
96.text: DealforceCRE uses a simple bid sheet versioning system to help you submit your bid when it's ready.1. To view your bid sheet, click View Bid Sheet on the Bid Overview page.2. You will now see something that looks like an excel document, but with just two columns - Bid and Notes.Bid is where you will enter your final bid amount for that line item. Line items are totaled by section.Notes is where you will enter any notes for that line item. Notes will be visible to the Bid Contact when you submit the bid.3. Every time you make a change to a bid sheet you will want to click Save Bid at the top of your screen. This will save all of your information without submitting it. 4. Bid sheets can be given nicknames to help you remember why you created that particular bid. Click Add Nickname to enter a short nickname.5. When your bid sheet is ready to be submitted, click the Submit Bid button. When you click that, a notification will be sent to the Bid Package Contact letting them know that they need to review the bid sheet. This also means that this version cannot be edited and a new one must be created if you wish to update any numbers.

97.subject: Bid Management
97.title: Creating a New Version
97.text: When you're ready to update your Bid Sheet, you'll create a new version. Your old version stays unchanged and will always be available.1. To create a new version, navigate to your bid sheet and click + New Version.2. A copy of your last version will be created, and that becomes the current version you're able to update.3. Update the version as you typically do, and then click Submit Bid to submit your bid or Save Bid if you'd like to come back later.4. To view past versions, click Version History. This will show you the versions you've submitted and the day they were submitted. Your current, unsubmitted version will show - Current next to it. Clicking a past version will show you a view-only look at that version.

98.subject: Bid Management
98.title: Sending RFIs
98.text: A Request For Information can be sent at any time by any bidder. To submit an RFI, visit your bid overview page and click.1. You'll be asked to provide a short subject and additional information for clarification. Provide as many details as possible.2. You also have the option to attach a file. This can be useful if you need to provide additional clarification with a supporting document.3. Once submitted, you'll see that your RFI has a status of Open and you have the ability to edit it by clicking the pencil icon.4. When you receive an RFI response via in app notification and/or email, you'll be able to click on the View RFI link. That email will include the response, but the response is also stored on your Bid Overview page.5. After you review the response, you may have additional questions. We recommend either submitting another RFI, or even easier, sending a comment via the bid overview page.6. You may see some RFIs that you did not submit, but are visible to you. This is because some RFIs can be shared with all bidders, including RFIs that you submit.

99.subject: Bid Management
99.title: Bid Updates
99.text: Bid Updates are similar to mass emails, except they are accessible via DealforceCRE.To see all Bid Updates that have been sent out, visit your Bid Overview and scroll to the bottom.By clicking the Eye icon, you can see the update text along with any files or folders that were attached.

100.subject: Bid Management
100.title: Commenting On A Bid
100.text: You can communicate with the bid package contact at any time by logging into DealforceCRE, visiting the Bid Overview page, and commenting on the left side.Anytime you send in a new comment or reply to a comment, the Bid Package Contact will receive a notification. Whenever the contact replies to a comment you sent in, you will receive an email and in app notification.

101.subject: Draws
101.title: Draw Permissions
101.text: The first step to setting up a draw is ensure you have the proper permissions. For Draws there are three possible permissions: No AccessReady OnlyRead / WriteUsers with 'Read Only' permissions cannot: Edit Draw SettingsCreate a DrawSubmit a DrawAdd Draw TodosAdd Vendors to the PDSAdd Categories on the Closing Documents tabRequest New Documents on the Closing Documents tabAs a lead draw contact, individuals responsible for creating and administering a Draw, you will need 'Read / Write' permissions.Read/write permissions should be reserved for the internal DealforceCRE user, or the individual preparing the draw information and documentation uploads.External users (lenders/bank contacts) are set up differently with fewer permissions, only allowing them to view the draws and download the documentation.Instructions for setting up external users for Draws:Draws for External Users

102.subject: Draws
102.title: The Closing Settlement
102.text: When the first Draw is created, it is created as a 'Closing Settlement' and is given a status of draft. When creating the Closing Settlement, you will also be able to link an existing Pay App to the Closing Settlement.To edit the Closing Settlement, click on the info icon to the right of the screen. The Closing Settlement is broken into five different sections: OverviewDraw Payment Distribution Settlement (PDS)Payment DocumentsClosing DocumentsActivities

103.subject: Draws
103.title: Overview
103.text: The Draw overview is the first tab you will see when you click on the information icon from a Draw in the Draw index. The overview is broken out into five primary sections. These are: Settlement DetailsSettlement ChecklistLatest ActivityPayment SummarySettlement TodosThe settlement details section shows very high level information pertaining to the draw (things like date created, estimated funding date, project name, and more) Underneath this settlement details section is a comments section. Next we have a settlement checklist, this shows whether the following four primary tasks have been completed: Settlement Approved by OwnerOwner PDS SignedSettlement Submitted to LenderSettlement Approved by LenderBeneath that we have the 'latest activity' section which shows the most recent activity. The payment summary in the top right shows: Revised Contract AmountPrevious Payments to DateClosing Settlement Balance to CompleteFinally, the settlement todos are in the bottom right corner of the overview page. Please note that the 'Submit Closing Settlement' and 'Download' buttons are viewable from this Draw overview, as well as all other pages of the draw.

104.subject: Draws
104.title: Draw Payment Distribution Schedule
104.text: Payment Distribution ScheduleThe Draw PDS pulls in each line item from the budget into an index. At the top of this page you have a search field to search through these tasks, and also an 'Additional Equity Required' amount at the top.In the top right you have an 'Add Company' button.Clicking this opens up the 'Add Vendor' window. From here, you can add new vendors which should appear on the Draw PDS. PaymentsAt the bottom of the Draw Payment Distribution Schedule is the 'Available Payments Index' What this does is show all available payments on this project. Here you can search for payments, filter payments, or event add new recorded payments or payment requests. It's important to note that prior to the creation of the closing settlement, users can link payments to budget task line items. Since the closing settlement is comprised of all the line items from the budget, any payments marked paid linked to these budget line items prior to the creation of the closing settlement, will automatically pull through into the closing settlement. Meaning that certain line items on the Draw Payment Distribution Schedule may already be linked to payments upon the creation of the closing settlement. Linking payments to budget tasksFor any line items on the Draw Payment Distribution Schedule that are not linked to payments, users should now create this link . Notice at the bottom of this page there is an 'Available Payments' section. To link a payment to a line item in the PDS, a user should simply locate the payment which corresponds to line item. Once located, scroll all the way to the right and locate the link icon. When you click this, the 'Link Payment' window will open. From here, you can choose a task to link the payment to. Please note that when linking payments, there is a disclaimer: "Payments can only be linked to a task that has the same company as the payment's payee."Users can also choose if the payment being linked is linked as a 'previous payment' or a 'closing settlement'. AdditionallyAdding PaymentsAdditionally, a user might find that a payment was never entered in the system, yet did occur and is now needed on the Draw Payment Distribution Schedule.

105.subject: Draws
105.title: Creating a Draw
105.text: To get started with Draws, the first thing you'll want to do is head over to the budget tab, and under the budget dropdown menu, click Draws. Once on the Draw page, start by clicking on the 'Draw Settings' button in the top right. This will open up the 'Draw Settings' window. From here you will set the approvers, signers and verifiers. For verifiers, please make sure you have a verifier for each document type, or if the chosen verifier will be responsible for all document types, simply leave the field as the 'All Document Types', which is the default field. Once all the settings are complete, click the 'save' button to create the Draw.

106.subject: Draws
106.title: Draw Feature Overview
106.text: Draw Feature1. LOGIN & PROJECT NAVIGATION:1.1 DealforceCRE users now have the ability to access project draws digitally in DealforceCRE. This feature overview explains user login, general app navigation, and draw documentation.To begin, log into DealforceCRE with your email and password:Once logged in, your available projects will display. Select the project by clicking on the project tile:1.2 On the project page, click on the 'Budget' tab at the top portion of the page. A few different options will be available in the dropdown list:Construction Contracts - Contract name, payee and original contract amount. Users with adequate permissions (usually internal developer users), can adjust the contract preferences within this feature. All available contracts for the project are displayed on this feature. Clicking the pencil icon allows edits:Internal users who set up/manage the contracts are able to edit basic contract details, change order details and pay app defaults, such as approvers, distribution, retainable, default required documents, signers and document verifiers:Construction Change Orders - Any change orders for the project will be visible in this section of the application and users with adequate permissions may add new construction change orders in this section:Pay Applications - Pay application section for the project. Users can view pay applications by clicking on the 'i' icon on the right side of the page, for any pay app they wish to view:Draws - Section for the closing settlement and all project draws:2. DRAWS FEATURE:2.1 To view draws for a project, select 'Draws' in the dropdown.Click the 'i' icon to open the closing settlement or draw overview page:2.2 The Draw is comprised of five tabs. These are: 1. Overview2. Draw Payment Distribution Schedule (PDS) 3. Payments4. Draw Documents5. Linked Pay Application6. Activities2.3 The Overview tab shown below, is comprised of the following sections: Draw DetailsGeneral Details about the drawDraw ChecklistChecklist showing the major steps to draw completionLatest ActivityActivity history on the draws (approvals, verifications, document uploads, etc)Payment SummaryAn overall mathematical break down of draw2. The 'Draw Payment Distribution Schedule' (PDS) shows previous payments to date, what’s on the current draw and what’s left to complete:3. All draw payments live on this tab, including all documentation such as invoices, cancelled checks, unconditional/conditional progress, reimbursable status, waiver status and other documentation:The 'Payments' section on a draw also features certain interactive icons:Reimbursable - Can be toggled 'Yes/No' by selecting. This action is usually performed by the internal user completing the draw in DealforceCRE.Document upload requirement - Clicking on this icon will change the requirement for the particular document upload for the line item selected.Document not required - A gray 'X' icon indicates that the document upload is not required for that specific column.Document upload window - Clicking the cloud icon opens up the 'Upload Documents' popup window. This is how supporting documentation is uploaded for the payments.Preview documents - Allows users to view/download the individual document selected for the payment line item.Information icon - Redirects users to the payment overview page.4. Linked Pay Application - If a pay app is linked to the draw, the data from the pay application SOV, PDS, and documentation can easily be accessed on this tab. 5. Activities - Similar to the 'Latest Activity' section on the 'Overview' tab, this section shows timestamps for actions on the draw, including approvals, signatures and document uploads. This is the draw's audit history.In addition to these sections, as with all tabs within a draw, there are options for viewing and downloading the draw details, in the top right portion of the draw:Draw DocumentDownloadDraw SummaryPayment Distribution Schedule PDFPayment Distribution Schedule CSVEntire DrawDownloading the draw document, summary, entire draw or the PDS, will execute a PDF download, which can be opened and/or downloaded in your browser, or a desktop PDF clientEntire Draw Download - Since an entire draw can include various supporting documentation, the entire draw document downloads as a ZIP file:The file must be extracted locally on the machine used and once opened, root folder will contain various folders within it, including the draw document, payment invoices, W9's if uploaded and applicable and any other documents uploaded and associated with the draw in DealforceCRE:Now that we've covered the draw feature, the next section focuses on pay applications in DealforceCRE:PAY APPLICATIONS:In addition to project draws, pay application are also completed in DealforceCRE. Similar to draws, users can view pay application details for projects and view/download documentation. First, start by navigating to the project. Next, click on the 'Budget' dropdown menu in the project navigation area, then click on the 'Pay Applications' option in the dropdown. This is the pay applications page, where users are able to see an index of all Pay Applications on a project. In the image below, we can see that there are two Pay Apps on this particular project. To view an individual Pay App, simply click on the 'info' icon to the right of the Pay App. This will take the user to the Pay App overview.The Pay App is comprised of five tabs. These are: OverviewSchedule of Values (SoV)Payment Distribution (PDS) Documentation andActivitiesThis step will focus solely on the Overview tab, which is seen below. The Overview tab is comprised of the following sections: Pay App DetailsGeneral Details about the Pay AppApplication ChecklistChecklist showing the major steps to Pay App completionLatest ActivityLatest Activity on the Pay AppDraw Approval Process, and Shows status of approval requestsPayment SummaryAn overall mathematical break down of Pay AppTo navigate to other parts of the Pay App, simply use the navigation tabs at the top of the screen. The Schedule of Values (SoV) shows all costs that have been allocated to different work items. Most notably, on this table we can see the contractual amount, amounts for previously submitted Pay Apps as well as the amount being allocated for this Pay App. Totals for everything appear at the bottom of the table. On the PDS, you can see how money is being distributed, and who it's being distributed to. In the first column is the name of the company, and then under 'Contract Amount' we can see the total contracted amount. Under 'Pay #1', we can see amounts allocated to previous Pay Apps, and then 'This Pay App' shows the amount being paid out in this pay app. The final three columns on this table show what's been paid to date, as well as any remaining balance. The documentation tab shows a breakdown of all required documentation for a Pay App. The green, yellow, red indicators at the top show what's been verified, what's awaiting verification, as well as anything that's rejected or incomplete. To view a document that's been uploaded click the eye icon. This will open the document preview screen. Users can scroll through uploaded documents using the 'Previous' and 'Next' buttons, or download the document with the 'download' button. Finally, if you wish to download every document, simply click on the 'Download All Documents' button in the top right, which will download a zip file with all of the pay app documentation.From any tab within the Pay App, a user can click the 'download' button in the top right to download any of the following options: If everything is needed for download, simply choose the 'Entire Pay Application' option. This will download the SoV, the PDS, and the Signed Pay App Document, and all back up documentation.

107.subject: Draws
107.title: Permissions for Lenders
107.text: The idea behind the pay applications feature in DealforceCRE, is that the lender/bank contact is given an external user account, and then they can log into DealforceCRE and view the draw(s) themselves, throughout the lifecycle of the draw process, until the contract is satisfied for the project.First, an internal user must create the external user as a contact within the directory, if the user is not already a contact in the system: If the contact is already in the directory, simply search for the contact in the directory and enable their app access. App access can be granted on the 'Permissions' tab within the contact record, by toggling on the 'Grant App Access' icon:When granting the user app access, some initial configuration needs to take place, to ensure that the user can view only the information related to their contract and pay application. A pre-defined role has been created, named 'Draws - External Role' which will give the user access access to only the features in the app shown below:Let's break this down a little bit further, to illustrate what these permissions actually mean within DealforceCRE; the user will be able to see/access the following features:Budget Contracts - The user can view the contract amount, however, they cannot edit the details. Editing the contract is done internally by the CRE developerBudget Change Orders - The user can view any change orders associated with the contract of the company for which they are a part ofBudget Pay Applications - Read only: the user will have full access to initiate pay applications, upload documents, download, view the schedule of value details and payment distribution scheduleBudget Pay Applications - Read only: the user will have full access to view pay applications, view uploaded documents, download, view the schedule of value details and payment distribution scheduleDraws - Read only: the user will have full access to view the closing settlements & draw(s), upload documents, download all draw/ pay application documentation (including all waivers/invoices/cancelled checks) and view linked pay apps.Projects which External User can access - This is where the internal user will choose all of the projects, which the lender/bank contact may access. In most cases, the user would only need access to one or maybe just a few projects. In this case, it's important to select 'Selected Projects' and type in the project(s) manually, select and save them here:Company Level Access - Typically in DealforceCRE, when an external user is given access to the application, they are only able to see things like Pay Apps, Payments and Contracts that belong to the company they're associated with. This is called 'Company Level Access'. Lenders are one of the only situations where you want to give them access to see all of these objects, regardless of the company they work for. Therefore, on the first page of the permissions window, the following option should also be set to 'All Companies'. Now when a user logs in they can navigate all Pay Apps on a project, regardless of what company they work for, and regardless of which company the Pay App belongs to.

108.subject: Draws
108.title: Draw/Pay Application Feature Guide
108.text: Draw_Pay Application Guide.pdfThis document may be shared with GC's/lenders. There are 3 sections:1. DEALFORCECRE LOGIN & PROJECT NAVIGATION2. DRAWS FEATURE3. PAY APPLICATIONS FEATUREGCs - should review parts 1 & 2 (pay applications & general setup/navigation)Lenders - should review parts 1 & 3 (draws & general setup/navigation)

109.subject: Payments
109.title: Add a contract
109.text: 1. Navigate to a Project, click on Payments and then scroll down and click Add Contract.2. Complete the Add Contract window with the necessary information including:Internal Point of Contact - This is the internal team member who will be responsible for approving payments against the contract.External Point of Contact - This is the external user the contracts will be assigned.Payee - The company or external user paid by the contract.Contract Name - The name used to identify your contract in the DealforceCRE system.Payment Terms - Customizable payment terms (ex: 10/25/25/40, 40/90/10, Custom)Net Payment - The number of day a payee must wait after a payment is requested.Notifications - Reminders and lien waiver user responsibility (only visible if 'Lien waivers required for all payments' is checked).Notes - Any additional information required for the contract.3. Click Next and then complete the Delivery Details for the payment. Once completed, click Save.

110.subject: Payments
110.title: Customize payment terms
110.text: 1. To add a custom payment term, click either Custom (%) or Custom ($) in the Payment Terms dropdown.2. The percentage fields must equal 100% and the dollar amount fields must equal the Contract Amount. Also, each of the fields must have a title.3. To add additional line items, click the Add Payment Term button, or to remove a line item, click the Trash icon.

111.subject: Payments
111.title: View and edit contract
111.text: 1. To view contract details on the Payment Tab, click on the Contract Name. 2. To edit contract details on the Payment Tab, click on the edit icon.

112.subject: Payments
112.topic: Requesting payments as an Internal User
112.title: Create an internal payment request
112.text: 1. There are two locations to request an internal payment, the first from the Project Payment tab, where contracts are added:2. The second location is from the global menu by selecting Payments > Payments:3. Complete the Request Payment window with the appropriate information including:Request Type - Pre-Close, Post-Close or Miscellaneous used to categorize the requests External Checkbox - Used to submit a request for an External UserRequestor - The original requestor of the payment (this is the person who approves and is responsible for the request)Project - The project associated with the payment requestContract - A contract if there's one associated with the requestPayee - The external user who will receive the payment (click the + New Contact if the contact isn't in the system)Amount - The payment totalEstimated Payment Date - When the payment needs to be madePayment Review - Choose to select a review status or send to another user for reviewDescription - Any additional information needed4. Complete the Payment Type tab, where you can choose whichever payment type applies to the payment.5. The final Notes tab includes a variety of fields depending on what type of request is being submitted. Has Invoice - Upload any invoice documentsHas Backup - Upload any backup documentsReimbursable - If the payment is reimbursableRefundable - If the payment is refundableUrgent Payment - Will send an immediate notification to the finance team for quick processingPrivate - Payment will only visible to the requestor and administratorsEarnest Money - If the payment is earnest money and will be payed out of a separate accountCAM Expense - Flags payment as a CAM expenseCommission Contingency Completed - Enter a date for this optionYardi Accounting - Marks a payment as part of Yardi accountingYardi GL Codes - Add one or more Yardi GL Codes to a paymentAdditional Notes - Add any additional notes6. Click Save and the payment request has been submitted!

113.subject: Payments
113.topic: Requesting payments as an Internal User
113.title: Request a payment on behalf of an external user
113.text: 1. To request a payment on behalf of an external user, click the External box on the Payment Request window. In this case, the Requestor will be assigned as an external user. 2. Next click the Project the request is for, which will open the Contracts dropdown and include any of the contracts available for that project.3. Once you select a contract, the Contract Details will appear along with the Payee and the Payment Amounts available.4. Once a Payment Amount has been requested or paid, the amount will grey out and become unavailable to select.5. The Estimated Payment Date is calculated based on the original contract Net Payment Terms. 6. Complete the Delivery tab with the Payee Details.7. Complete the Notes tab with the appropriate checks and uploads. For external payment requests, backup documents are required.

114.subject: Payments
114.title: Set payment admin permissions
114.text: 1. The ability to process and approve payment requests is limited to users that have Process and Approve permissions, which are set in the User Details.2. The other available permissions are:No Requests - The user can not request any paymentsRequest and Review Only - Can submitted requests and review requests but not Process and ApproveProcess and Approve - Can request and Process and Approve3. A user that has Process and Approve permissions can then set what statuses they want to receive notifications for. The statuses include:New - New Internal Request that is ready to be reviewed by the internal finance teamProcessed - Internal or External Request to be reviewed by second layer of internal finance teamApproved - Internal or External Request to be approved by second layer of internal finance team and ready to be paidHeld - Request has been stopped temporarilyPaid - Request has been paidCancelled - Request has been stopped indefinitelySubmitted - New External Request that needs to be reviewed by an Internal Point of ContactReviewed (Paid per Contract/Pay at COE/Pay on Draw/Pay upon Receipt) - When an External Request is approved by an Internal Point of Contact and ready to be reviewed by the internal finance team

115.subject: Payments
115.title: The Payment Review Process
115.text: The general process for all externally submitted payment requests (or payment requests marked External) is as follows:1. Payment submitted by external user. Payment request given status of Submitted.2. Internal Point of Contact for contract associated with that payment request is notified that a payment request has been submitted against a contract they are responsible for. When they visit that payment request, they will be asked to mark the payment as Reviewed.*Note - If the Internal Point of Contact were to submit a payment request on an external user's behalf by clicking "External", the status will skip Submitted and go right to Reviewed.3. The payment is now ready for Processing. Any user with the "Process and Approve" permission set and the notification set to "Reviewed" will receive a notification that they need to process the payment. This could mean that a check is written, or that an ACH transfer is set up.4. After the payment is marked as Processed, it now goes to the user that needs to Approve the payment method. This is typically the final check to ensure that the check or ACH transfer is correct. The approver will click "Approve" in the top right.5. The last step is for the payment request to be marked Paid, meaning that the check has been dropped in the mail or the transfer of funds has been initiated. Note that this may automatically trigger a Lien Waiver to be sent.

117.subject: Payments
117.title: Change Orders and Reimbursements
117.text: a payment is marked as a reimbursable & a project has sold/closed, it’s important to go back and check reimbursable status to ensure all payments & refunds have been processed. To do this, you’ll navigate to the payments tab of a project. Next, you’ll click on ‘filters’ at the payments section. Choose ‘reimbursement status’. You’ll want to filter by incomplete, and then by partial. From here, you can see the payments that are marked as reimbursable, whether that be incomplete, partial, or complete.

118.subject: Payments
118.title: Change Orders
