121.subject: Payments
121.title: Part III - Submitting a Payment Request

123.subject: Pay Applications
123.title: Overview
123.text: As you know, pay applications and draws are used to fund many commercial real estate projects. This process is handled through various documentation such as the Schedule of Values (“SoV”), the Payment Distribution Schedule (“PDS”), a closing settlement, and any other documentation which the bank requires, such as lien waivers. Typically, these documents are created and managed by using spreadsheets, and PDF documents. DealforceCRE now houses this entire process directly in the application. This helps to ensure that the pay application balances, that only fully executed change orders are included on the pay application, and that everything stays organized in one central location. To get started with pay applications, an internal user will begin by filling out the ‘Pay Application Defaults’ on the 'Construction Contract'.

124.subject: Pay Applications
124.title: Payment Application Defaults
124.text: When filing out a construction contract under the budget tab, you will notice there are five sections to the contract: Budget, Construction Contracts, Construction Change Orders, Pay Applications, and Draws.For this example, navigate to the 'Construction Contracts' section and either create a new construction contract by clicking 'Add Construction Contract', or edit an existing one by clicking the pencil icon.In the Contract Contracts section, the payee and the contract amount are two fields that will tie into the Payment Application feature. That is to say, the pay application should be based on the total contract amount, and the payee will be the General Contractor working on the project, and will be the only external user that has access to payment applications as they are created. Of course the second section of the construction contract window, the pay app defaults, also relates to the pay application. Here you will set the retainage amount for the pay applications to be entered against this contract. You can also choose the distribution of 'Owner', 'Architect', or 'Contractor'.Next, you'll choose any needed approvers on the pay application. Additional approvers can be added, as can an approving order. Next you'll choose the signers of the pay app, by default one signer for the General Contractor needs to be selected, and one signer from the Owner (internal CRE developer). Here, a signer order can be set as well, if necessary. Next, you can add verifiers. Verifiers, as the name implies will be the individuals who will need to verify required documentation. Additional verifiers can be added. Notice there is also a 'Document Types' field paired with the verifier field. Document types allow a user to choose which types of documents the user is responsible for verifying. For example, you might choose that one user is responsible for verifying all pre-liens and invoices, while another is in charge of all waivers and other documentation, which might look something like this:It's important to note that each document type must have a verifier assigned. Most pay applications will consist of just one verifier and this is the case, the default will be 'All Document Types'For this example, we'll simply choose one user, and we'll make this user responsible for all document types:Once the pay app defaults are completed, you may continue filling out the rest of the construction contract details and save the contract. Now that this part is done, we're ready to begin our first payment application for this project.

125.subject: Pay Applications
125.topic: GC External User Account Creation & Permissions
125.title: Creating New External User Account for GC
125.text: The idea behind the pay applications feature in DealforceCRE, is that the General Contractor contact is given an external user account, and then the GC can log into DealforceCRE and enter the pay app(s) themselves, throughout the lifecycle of the draw process, until the contract is satisfied for the project, meaning that the contractor received all payments and the lender has paid the developer everything in the contract.To accomplish this, parties entered on the construction contract covered in the previous topic, will need access to DealforceCRE, including the GC, who will need to have external user access to DealforceCRE. First, an internal user must create the external user as a contact within the directory, if the user is not already a contact in the system: If the contact is already in the directory, simply search for the GC contact in the directory and enable their app access. App access can be granted on the 'Permissions' tab within the contact record, by toggling on the 'Grant App Access' icon:When granting the user app access, some initial configuration needs to take place, to ensure that the GC can view only the information related to their contract and pay application. A pre-defined role has been created, named 'Pay App/Draws' which will give the user access to only the features in the app shown below:Let's break this down a little bit further, to illustrate what these permissions actually mean within DealforceCRE; the user will be able to see/access the following features:Signature Requests - Read/Write: the user will have access to sign anything needed of them throughout the pay application processApprovals & Verifications - Read/Write: the user will have access to approve anything needed of them throughout the pay application processBudget Contracts - The user can view the contract amount, however, they cannot edit the details. Editing the contract is done internally by the CRE developerBudget Change Orders - The user can view any change orders associated with the contract of the company for which they are a part ofBudget Pay Applications - Read/Write: the user will have full access to initiate pay applications, upload documents, approve, download, fill out the schedule of value details and balance the payment distribution schedule against the contract amount. Projects Which External User (GC) can Access - This is where the internal user will choose all of the projects, which the GC may access. In most cases, the user would only need access to one or maybe just a few projects. In this case, it's important to select 'Selected Projects' and type in the project(s) manually, select and save them here:Company Level Access - this is a very important step in the external user account set-up process. In most cases, the GC should only be able see their own company's Pay Apps. However, if the user needs to see pay applications for the project, 'All Companies' can be selected. Again, this is a highly uncommon scenario, so 'Their Company Only' should be the necessary selection here

126.subject: Pay Applications
126.title: Creating a Payment Application
126.text: Once the external user logs into DealforceCRE, they can access the Pay Apps feature by clicking on the 'Budget' tab on a projects which they have access to and then clicking on 'Pay Applications' Doing so will take the user to the 'Pay Applications' page:To begin, click the 'New Pay Application' button. The 'New Pay Application' window will open. From here you'll need to choose a contract that the Pay App is associated to. If this the final Pay App to be submitted, the user would need to check the box for 'Submit as Final Contract Pay Application' Once a contract is chosen, click 'Save.'Once the user clicks 'Save' the pay application will be created, and the user will be taken to the pay app itself.

127.subject: Pay Applications
127.title: Pay App Overview
127.text: When the Pay App is first created, the user will be taken to the Pay App itself. The Pay App is comprised of a five tabs. These are: OverviewSchedule of Values (SoV)Payment Distribution (PDS) DocumentationActivitiesThis step will focus solely on the 'Overview' tab, displayed below: The Overview tab is comprised of the following sections: Pay App DetailsGeneral Details about the Pay AppApplication ChecklistChecklist showing the major steps to Pay App completionLatest ActivityActivity history on the Pay App (approvals, verifications, document uploads, etc)Draw Approval Process Shows status of approval requestsPayment SummaryAn overall mathematical break down of Pay AppIn addition to these sections, as with all tabs from the Pay App, there are some additional options in the top right portion of the Pay App, depending on the current status of the Pay App. One is 'Submit Pay App' and one is 'Download'. These buttons display when the Pay App is in draft. When the Pay App is submitted/signed, users will be given two more options: 'Reset Application' and 'Pay Application Document'Reset Application - After a pay app has been signed, there are times when the SOV and PDS need to be updated. Reset Application will show only if the Pay App status is not Draft. If a user clicks the reset app button, the Pay App's status will change back to 'draft', and any approvals and signatures will be nullified. This allows a user to make adjustments to the PDS/SoV and resubmit the app for approval and signature again. The data and numerical values that were previously entered will still exist.Pay Application Document - Displays the Pay App Document file overview in DealforceCREThe following options are available under 'Download.' From here, PDF versions are created from Document downloads:Pay application - Downloads the current Pay AppSchedule of Values - Downloads the SOV onlyPayment Distribution Schedule - PDF of the Pay App PDSPayment Distribution Schedule - CSV of the Pay App PDSEntire Pay Application - Downloads all information for the current and all previous Pay Apps

128.subject: Pay Applications
128.title: Schedule of Values
128.text: We will now cover the second tab, the Schedule of Values ("SoV").The SoV shows all work items, and costs from the beginning to the end of the project. On this tab as well, we also show the entire contract price at the top portion of the page. Until the full contract price has been allocated, the amount will show as incomplete. Ultimately these set values will be used to actually allocate funds according to the payment distribution schedule, when different work items are completed. The pay app shows how a job is progressing, and helps companies compare projected costs against actual costs. It will be up to the external filling out the SoV on work is either divided into smaller portions (line items) or the work might be less specific and therefore certain portions of work might be grouped together as one line item.The table seen on the SoV tab is of course for entering these work items / line items. To add your first line item, click on the 'Add Description of Work' button in the top right. When you do so, the 'Add Description of Work' window will appear. From here, you will simply enter in a name for description of work, and a contract value. If retention does not need to apply to the item entered, the user may check 'Do not apply retainage'.**The 'Description of Work' field is a dropdown, which pulls values from a list created in lists and tools. These 'Pay App Description of Work' items are created by adding a phase code and a name.**From here, you will simply enter in a name for description of work, and a contract value. In this example, I have chosen 'General Conditions' , which has a phase code pre-populated. Once done click 'Save' and the description of work will be added. When a user adds these items in the schedule of values, the total of the schedule of values should match the original contract amount. Here's an overly simplified version of what a pay app looks like once multiple line items are added. Note the incomplete at the top This is because the amount allocated in the schedule of values ($99,900) is $100 less than the total contract amount ($100,000)Note if I add $100 to insurance, the icon will change to complete, because the schedule of values is now at $100,000, which matches the contract amount. And note the bottom row totals everything. On the schedule of values you can also include full executed change orders. This button in the top right indicates that there is one fully executed change order which can be placed in the schedule of values. Let's click this and pull the one change order in. This change order was for $552.50, which brings the total of the Schedule of Values to $100,552.50. At this point the Schedule of Values will still balance and show 'Complete' because change orders are in addition to the original contract amount. Additionally, on the Schedule of Values, there are also columns for 'This Period' and 'Stored Materials' Because there are often multiple pay applications on a project, when each one is submitted, the General Contractor will state how much the pay application is allocating to a particular description of work in 'this period'.In other words, you might have $12,000 allocated to landscaping, but if only 1/2 of the project is complete, this pay might only account for $6,000 this period. In the example below, we see a 'this period' all set to 50% of the total Schedule of Values. Notice there are columns for Total completed, percent complete, and balance to finish. Finally, we see the total retainage in the far right column. Because allocating 50% of all costs to this pay application, we can see that the balance to finish is exactly equal to the total completed. This is of course an over simplified example, but it should help to illustrate how this feature works. At this point, we can consider this Schedule of Values completed. Let's now move on to the Payment Distribution Schedule, or the PDS.

129.subject: Pay Applications
129.title: The Payment Distribution Schedule
129.text: If the Schedule of Values is the type of work to do on a project, the The Payment Distribution Schedule, or the PDS, outlines WHO is doing that work. The (PDS) shows previous payments to date, what’s due and what’s left to complete. And all these numbers have to match up with the SoV.To begin learning the PDS, let's start by analyzing the columns here on this table. From the left we have company, location and phone, which are all columns related to the company doing the work. Next we have the contract amount, which should be the same from the schedule of values, you then have a column for change orders, then a total final contract column which adds change orders and the contract amount together. Next you have the payment being distributed on this pay app, payment %, you have the total that's been paid to date, the paid to date %, and finally the current balance. Now that you know what columns are on this table, let's begin adding line items to the PDS. You do so by clicking on the 'Add Subcontractor/Supplier' button in the top right. When you do so, the 'Add Subcontractor/Supplier' window will open. Start by adding the name of the company that is doing the work. This field pulls from the global directory. If the company you're looking for isn't in the directory, click '+ New Company' to add it. Here, we're adding the line item which corresponds with the 'superintendent' line item from the SoV. Repeat this process until all the line items are finished. Notice in the example below we now have one line item for each item from the SoV. In the real world, the PDS will not always be so straight forward. In many cases you might have multiple companies (therefore multiple line items) completing one line item from the SoV. Also note, the 'Totals Match SOV' is 'complete.' This is because the contract amounts on the PDS match the amounts from the SoV. Finally, also note that the change order amount for $552.50 has been added in the change order column on the 'weather protect' line. Even though we've entered all the line items at this time, notice the 'Payments Distributed' still shows as incomplete with a total of $45,248.63 (remember that's the amount from the SoV that we stated we're paying THIS pay app). This is because we haven't actually allocated any funds yet. At this point, we've only stated what the contract amount is. Notice our 'payment' column is still all $0's. Let's fix this by entering the amounts being paid out. Before we do that, let's revisit retainage. Remember - retainage (or retention) is an amount of money that is withheld from the sub contractors until the end of the project. Retainage is usually 10%, but can vary from project to project.In this example I set retainage as 10%. This should be the same amounts we said were getting paid out from the SoV, minus the retainage amount from each line item. Notice in the example below, each item is 10% less than it was on the SoV. Notice there is also a column for 'Confirmation'. This is a checkbox for the General Contractor to specify whether or not they are 100% sure the amount entered will not change. Perhaps the check has already been written or the payment has already been made. However, since payment amounts CAN change after a pay app is submitted, most of these would be left unlocked, which would allow the user to move money around even after the pay app is submitted. A GC can move money around as needed, as long as the PDS still balances.This way, when the GC goes to fill out pay app 2, this check box confirmation does two things: locks the payment amount (which you can just unlock by clicking the confirmation button) changes the payment confirmation status FOR THE PREVIOUS PAYMENT. But if you go make pay app 2, you'll see that the confirmations are incomplete. You can complete pay app 1 payments from pay app 2... that's how it's intended to workIn this example, I have confirmed the first two payments only and left the remaining amounts unchecked. Once all the balancing indicators at the top show 'complete' the pay app is ready to be submitted. Click the 'Submit Pay App' button in the top right. Enter in a date for 'period' and a 'GC project number'Then click 'send for signature'Assuming you have no errors, the pay app will be submitted successfully.**Possible submission error** The PDS payment total for This Pay App has to match the calculated payment amount from the SOVThe error below will display upon submission: And then also, if the contract value (including change orders) on the SOV is different from the contract amount (plus change orders). You will also get an error when trying to submit. In the next step we will cover the approval / signature process.

130.subject: Pay Applications
130.title: Pay App Approvals / Signatures
130.text: Once the pay app has been submitted, it's now time to for the internal team to approve the pay app. Remember, the approver(s) of the pay app is set on the construction contract in the pay app defaults section. In this case, I have just one approver. In this case, the approver will get a notification saying their approval is being requested on a pay app. When they click the notification, they will be taken to the pay app overview with an approval / reject banner at the top. Once approved, the pay app will then go then be sent (via Docusign) to the signers. At this point the contractor (Kellen External) would Docusign the Pay App, and then the owner (Kellen Wesley) would sign the Pay App. On the overview of the Pay App, you can see all approvals and signature requests in the history section.This information is also visible on the 'Activities' tab.Also, in the top of the Pay App overview, you should see a 'Pay Application Document' button. Clicking this takes the user to the signed pay app. Which is comprised of the signed document, the Schedule of Values, and the Payment Distribution Schedule.

131.subject: Pay Applications
131.title: Documentation
131.text: Now that the Pay App has been approved and signed, and also concurrently with this process, users are ready to start uploading all required documentation. Exactly which verifications are needed on a Pay App are at first determined by the Pay App defaults on the construction contract. By default, all of these types of documents will be checked (required) on a pay app. To not require a certain type of document for all line items in a pay app, simply uncheck the box here. Here on the documentation tab, the contractor would be responsible for uploading all required documentation. In this case, since we left all 'Default required documents' checked on the pay app default, the contractor is responsible for uploading Pre-Liens, Conditional Progress Waivers, Unconditional Progress Waivers, Invoices and Other Documentation. You can manually override document requirement defaults by clicking on the (red 'x') in the pay application, which will gray out that upload icon, indicating that the document is no longer required. To upload a document simply click on the cloud icon. The Pre-Lien upload window is the one upload window which looks different from the rest. Here, you must choose a date, an amount, a sub contractor, and then upload the file itself. Please also add notes if they are required. Once done, 'click save'. Now that one document has been uploaded we can see that there is now 1 'awaiting' document. Which leaves 43 (out of 45) documents left to upload (remember we turned the requirement for one off). Please also note, that once a document has been uploaded, there are now new icons next to that document. We have an 'Eye' icon and an 'info' icon. Clicking the 'eye' icon opens up the document quick view window. From here, the user could download the document, as well as toggle between other documentation by clicking on the Previous and Next arrows. The remaining documentation types are simply a file upload field. At this point, we'll upload all remaining documentation. Once everything is uploaded you should see 'incomplete' indicator at the top at 0. Additionally, throughout a construction project, there will be suppliers who are owed money. And proof of payment and other documentation might also be needed for these suppliers. These are handled in the bottom section of the documentation tab, in the 'supplier documents' section. To get started adding suppliers, simply click the 'Add Supplier' button to the right. The 'Add Supplier' window will open. From this window. The user will enter in the date, amount, sub contractor if there is one, enter in the company, upload documents, and finally, enter in the supplier contact details (name, email and phone number). These items, just like the documentation above, will appear in a table below. Notice now there is 1 incomplete item and one awaiting. This is because here on the supplier lines you have the the original document uploaded, but then you can also upload a waiver for the payment amount. Essentially, this means that two documents could be required for each supplier added in this section. When suppliers log payments, it's important that they add their documentation for the Pay App. Instruct them to upload their lien waivers & amounts paid. To do this, click on the + sign.From this window the user will allocate a portion (or whole), upload waiver if needed, and choose the waiver type. Once entered, the incomplete should now show 0. And the awaiting should show as 2, since there are now two documents waiting on verification. Please note, a user can now click 'download all' in the top right to download a zip file, with pdfs, of all documentation. Repeat this process until all suppliers have been added. Once all required documentation, and all suppliers have been added, you should have 0 incomplete for the sub contractors, as well as 0 incomplete for the suppliers. At this point, we are ready to move onto the verification portion of the process. At this point this Pay App is 100% completed, and a draw could be processed at this time using the information herein contained. The draw process itself will be details in the Draws subject.

132.subject: Pay Applications
132.title: Verifications
132.text: Remember, on the Construction Contract in the Pay App defaults section, you can specify who the verifiers are. These verifiers might be an employee from the Development company, or multiple users.In this case, Graham Davis is the only verifier on this Pay App. And his document type was not set to specific documents, instead, he is responsible for verifying all documents. Each time a document is uploaded on the documentation tab, Graham Davis will receive a notification asking for his verification. When the user clicks on the 'Review and Verify' link, he will be taken here: From here, he would either verify or reject the document. If he were to reject the document, he would be prompted to enter some comments as to why it was rejected. Once verified, the verification will show in the file history. All verifiers would follow this process for all remaining documents which they should verify. Once verified, the Contractor will receive a notification stating such. Once all verifications have taken place, the documentation tab of the pay app overview should look something like this. Notice all the green checkmarks next to each required document, the 22 verified at the top, the 2 verified supplier documents at the bottom, and each of the waiting indicators are at 0.

133.subject: Pay Applications
133.title: Subsequent and Final Pay Apps
133.text: As you know, During the funding phases of a project, there are likely multiple draws and thusly multiple Pay Apps which exist on a project. Remember, in the Schedule of values we created in this subject, we allocated 100% of the total contract amount to the various line items form the Schedule of Values, however, if you recall, we did not allocate 100% of those funds to the various sub contractors on the first Pay App. And that is of course typical with how the projects pan out. In the first Pay App on this example, for simplicity, we allocated about 50%, which would essentially state that half of the work was done on the project, and now payments to the General Contractor and the Sub Contractors is now due. In this section, we'll briefly add another Pay App so that 100% of the total from the SoV will have been allocated to the various PDS's from the two Pay Apps. Also, remember in the first Pay App, we had to back out the retainage in order to get the Pay App to balance, this was because the retainage is withheld (not paid) until the end of the project. And that's why when we click the 'Add Payment Application' button from the Pay Application index on the Pay Application's tab, there is a checkbox that says 'Submit as Final Contract Pay Application' With a disclaimer saying 'Check this box if this pay application will be the final request for payment against this contract. Retainage will be unlocked and available to be billed'To keep things simple in this example, we'll only be submitting 2 Pay Apps, which will account for 100% of the total contract amount. So during this time, we will check this box and proceed with the pay app. On the SoV for this second Pay App, the values for this period would be entered. Remember, for this example we're simply allocating the remaining 50% of the contract totals. Next, we'll set the distribution amounts on the PDS of this second Pay App. Remember, since this is the final Pay App on this project, you'll need to ensure the retainage amount which has been withheld up to this point, is now being factored into each payment being distributed here. In our case if the total amount for a line item is $2,000, this means that in the first pay app, half of the payment would have been $1,000, which we would have withheld at that time (10%), resulting in a distributed payment of $900. So this means on the pay app the total would be the remaining balance left to be paid out. Which would be $1,100Final Pay App Payment = (Total Contract Amount - all previous pay apps) Or in our case: ($2,000 - $900) Which would result in our final payment being: $1,100And since this is the final Pay App, the submitter should also check the box to confirm all remaining payments from both this Pay App, as well as the unconfirmed payments from the previous Pay App. Once all final payments have been entered (including retainage) the indicators at the top should balance like so, please note the payment confirmations are also complete. At this point, this second, and final pay app is ready to be submitted. Click the 'Submit Pay App' button in the top right part of the page. Then, choose the period and the GC Project Number. This Pay App will of course now have a status of 'Submitted'. The Pay App will go to the approvers, and then the signers just like in the previously submitted Pay App. Once all the approvals and signatures have taken place, the Pay App will still be awaiting any required documentation to be uploaded for this Pay App. Once all the required documentation is uploaded, the Pay App is now finished and the Pay App overview should look something like this, notice everything in the 'Application Checklist' has a green checkmark, and the 'Balance To Finish' line item in the payment summary is now at $0. Now, the users could the download button to down this second Pay App's Pay App Document, the SoV, the PDS, or the Entire Payment Application. The absolute final step in this process, would be for the verifier to verify the documents uploaded in the second Pay App, which is a process that is explained in prior steps.

134.subject: Payment Applications for External Users
134.title: Creating The Payment Application
134.text: The idea behind Pay Apps is that the General Contract will be made an external user, and then the GC can log into DealforceCRE and enter the Pay App themselves. Next you have the payment being distributed on this pay app, you have the total that's been paid to date, the paid to date %, and finally the current balance. Now that you know what columns are on this table, let's begin adding line items to the PDS. You do so by clicking on the 'Add Subcontractor/Supplier' button in the top right. When you do so, the 'Add Subcontractor/Supplier' window will open. Start by adding the name of the company that is doing the work. This field pulls from the global directory. If the company you're looking for isn't in the directory, click '+ New Company' to add it. Here, we're adding the line item which corresponds with the 'superintendent' line item from the SoV. Repeat this process until all the line items are finished. Notice in the example below we now have one line item for each item from the SoV. In the real world, the PDS will not always be so straight forward. In many cases you might have multiple companies (therefore multiple line items) completing one line item from the SoV. Also note, the 'Totals Match SOV' is 'complete.' This is because my contract amounts on the PDS match the amounts from the SoV. Finally, also note that the change order amount for $552.50 has been added in the change order column on the 'weather protect' line. Even though we've entered all the line items at this time, notice the 'Payments Distributed' still shows as incomplete with a total of $45,248.63 (remember that's the amount from the SoV that we stated we're paying THIS pay app). This is because we haven't actually allocated any funds yet. At this point, we've only stated what the contract amount is. Notice our 'payment' column is still all $0's. Let's fix this by entering the amounts being paid out. Before we do that, let's revisit retainage. Remember - retainage (or retention) is an amount of money that is withheld from the sub contractors until the end of the project. Retainage is usually 10%, but can vary from project to project.In this example I set retainage as 10%. This should be the same amounts we said were getting paid out from the SoV, minus the retainage amount from each line item. Notice in the example below, each item is 10% less than it was on the SoV. Notice there is also a column for 'confirmation' This is a checkbox for the General Contractor to specify whether or not they are 100% sure the amount entered will not change. Perhaps the check has already been written or the payment has already been made. However, since payment amounts CAN change after a pay app is submitted, most of these would be left unlocked, which would allow the user to move money around even after the pay app is submitted. This way, when the GC goes to fill out pay app 2, this check box confirmation does two things: locks the payment amount (which you can just unlock by clicking the confirmation button) changes the payment confirmation status FOR THE PREVIOUS PAYMENT. But if you go make pay app 2, you'll see that the confirmations are incomplete. You can complete pay app 1 payments from pay app 2... that's how it's intended to workIn this example, I have confirmed the first two payments only and left the remaining amounts unchecked. Once all the balancing indicators at the top show 'complete' the pay app is ready to be submitted. Click the 'Submit Pay App' button in the top right. Enter in a date for 'period' and a 'GC project number'Then click 'send for signature'Assuming you have no errors, the pay app will be submitted successfully. In the next step we will cover the approval / signature process. **Possible submission errors** The PDS payment total for This Pay App has to match the calculated payment amount from the SOVwill show this error upon submission: And then also, if the contract value (including change orders) on the SOV is different from the contract amount (plus change orders) you will also get an error when trying to submit.

137.subject: Payment Applications for External Users
137.title: Documentation
137.text: Now that the Pay App has been approved and signed, and also concurrently with this process, users are ready to start uploading all required documentation. Exactly which verifications are needed on a Pay App are at first determined by the Pay App defaults on the construction contract. By default, all of these types of documents will be checked (required) on a pay app. To not require a certain type of document for all line items in a pay app, simply uncheck the box here. Here on the documentation tab, the contractor would be responsible for uploading all required documentation. In this case, since we left all 'default required documents' checked on the pay app default, the contractor is responsible for uploading Pre-Liens, Conditional Progress Waivers, Unconditional Progress Waivers, Invoices and Other Documentation You can manually override document requirement defaults by clicking on the (red x) in the pay application, which will gray out that upload icon, indicating that the document is no longer required. To upload a document simply click on the cloud icon. The Pre-Lien upload window is the one upload window which looks different from the rest. Here, you must choose a date, an amount, a sub contractor, and then upload the file itself. Please also add notes if they are required. Once done, 'click save'. Now that one document has been uploaded we can see that there is now 1 'awaiting' document. Which leaves 43 (out of 45) documents left to upload (remember we turned the requirement for one off). Please also note, that once a document has been uploaded, there are now new icons next to that document. We have an 'Eye' icon and an 'info' icon. Clicking the 'eye' icon opens up the document quick view window. From here, the user could download the document, as well as toggle between other documentation by clicking on the Previous and Next arrows. The remaining documentation types are simply a file upload field. At this point, we'll upload all remaining documentation. Once everything is uploaded you should see 'incomplete' indicator at the top at 0. Additionally, throughout a construction project, there will be suppliers who are owed money. And proof of payment and other documentation might also be needed for these suppliers These are handled in the bottom section of the documentation tab, in the 'supplier documents' section. To get started adding suppliers, simply click the 'Add Supplier' button to the right. The 'Add Supplier' window will open. From this window. The user will enter in the date, amount, sub contractor if there is one, enter in the company, upload documents, and finally, enter in the supplier contact details (name, email and phone number). These items, just like the documentation above, will appear in a table below. Notice now there is 1 incomplete item and one awaiting. This is because here on the supplier lines you have the the original document uploaded, but then you can also upload a waiver for the payment amount. Essentially, this means that two documents could be required for each supplier added in this section. Clicking on the gray plus sign to the far right will allow you to allocate a certain portion of the total to this particular pay app. You do this in the 'Confirm Payment Amount' window. From this window the user will allocate a portion (or whole), upload waiver if needed, and choose the waiver type. Once entered, the incomplete should now show 0. And the awaiting should show as 2, since there are now two documents waiting on verification. Please note, a user can now click 'download all' in the top right to download a zip file, with pdfs, of all documentation. Repeat this process until all suppliers have been added. Once all required documentation, and all suppliers have been added, you should have 0 incomplete for the sub contractors, as well as 0 incomplete for the suppliers. At this point, we are ready to move onto the verification portion of the process. At this point this Pay App is 100% completed, and a draw could be processed at this time using the information herein contained. The draw process itself will be details in the Draws subject.

138.subject: Payment Applications for External Users
138.title: Subsequent and Final Pay Apps
138.text: As you know, During the funding phases of a project, there are likely multiple draws and thusly multiple Pay Apps which exist on a project. Remember, in the Schedule of values we created in this subject, we allocated 100% of the total contract amount to the various line items form the Schedule of Values, however, if you recall, we did not allocate 100% of those funds to the various sub contractors on the first Pay App. And that is of course typical with how the projects pan out. In the first Pay App on this example, for simplicity, we allocated about 50%, which would essentially state that half of the work was done on the project, and now payments to the General Contractor and the Sub Contractors is now due. In this section, we'll briefly add another Pay App so that 100% of the total from the SoV will have been allocated to the various PDS's from the two Pay Apps. Also, remember in the first Pay App, we had to back out the retainage in order to get the Pay App to balance, this was because the retainage is withheld (not paid) until the end of the project. And that's why when we click the 'Add Payment Application' button from the Pay Application index on the Pay Application's tab, there is a checkbox that says 'Submit as Final Contract Pay Application' With a disclaimer saying 'Check this box if this pay application will be the final request for payment against this contract. Retainage will be unlocked and available to be billed'To keep things simple in this example, we'll only be submitting 2 Pay Apps, which will account for 100% of the total contract amount. So during this time, we will check this box and proceed with the pay app. On the SoV for this second Pay App, the values for this period would be entered. Remember, for this example we're simply allocating the remaining 50% of the contract totals. Next, we'll set the distribution amounts on the PDS of this second Pay App. Remember, since this is the final Pay App on this project, you'll need to ensure the retainage amount which has been withheld up to this point, is now being factored into each payment being distributed here. In our case if the total amount for a line item is $2,000, this means that in the first pay app, half of the payment would have been $1,000, which we would have withheld at that time (10%), resulting in a distributed payment of $900. So this means on the pay app the total would be the remaining balance left to be paid out. Which would be $1,100Final Pay App Payment = (Total Contract Amount - all previous pay apps) Or in our case: ($2,000 - $900) Which would result in our final payment being: $1,100And since this is the final Pay App, the submitter should also check the box to confirm all remaining payments from both this Pay App, as well as the unconfirmed payments from the previous Pay App. Once all final payments have been entered (including retainage) the indicators at the top should balance like so, please note the payment confirmations are also complete. At this point, this second, and final pay app is ready to be submitted. Click the 'Submit Pay App' button in the top right of the page. Then, choose the period and the GC Project Number. This Pay App will of course now have a status of 'Submitted'. The Pay App will go to the approvers, and then the signers just like in the previously submitted Pay App. Once all the approvals and signatures have taken place, the Pay App will still be awaiting any required documentation to be uploaded for this Pay App. Once all the required documentation is uploaded, the Pay App is now finished and the Pay App overview should look something like this, notice everything in the 'Application Checklist' has a green checkmark, and the 'Balance To Finish' line item in the payment summary is now at $0. Now, the users could the download button to down this second Pay App's Pay App Document, the SoV, the PDS, or the Entire Payment Application. And that's it. You're done!

139.subject: Budgets
139.title: Part I - Introduction
139.text: What is it? DealforceCRE has a feature for tracking budgets over the lifetime of a project. Why? Having the budget within DealforceCRE allows for better communication and oversight over the budget as it moves through its three life-cycle phases: original pre-close budgetcurrent pre-close budgetand the original post close budgetAdditionally, the budget feature also has a vital contingency and approval system integrated through it. This will help to ensure that the budget is moving through proper approval channels as soft costs, hard costs, and contingency balances change over time. How it works? Now that we’ve gone over the why, let’s talk about how to use it. Start by going into a project and clicking on the ‘Budget’ tab, a drop-down menu will appear with the following options: You will notice that there are "Budget" and "New Budget" options. This is because there is the ability to have multiple budgets in a single project.For now, we’re only going to be using the ‘Budget’ page, which is the default budget.

140.subject: Budgets
140.title: Part II - Budget Page Layout
140.text: Budget Page LayoutThe budget page is broken down into a few key areas. Starting at the top left, you have the overall project budget section. This is a summary of the soft costs, hard costs, original pre-close budget, current pre-close budget, and the original post close budget. Just to the top right, you have a link / button.Clicking this is a good place to begin working on your budget, as it’s where you set the soft cost contingency and the hard cost contingency amount for the project. You can also change the name of your budget from here.In the top right, we have budget approvals. Here is where we track whether or not each phase of the budget has been approved. Moving downward on the page we have two important sections: Soft Cost Budget (an index / breakdown of individual soft cost line items, and totals) Hard Cost Budget (an index / breakdown of individual hard cost line items, and totals) And finally, we have a few useful tools / buttons which are located just to the top right of the soft cost budget section. Now that we know where everything is, let’s build a budget, and use all the features from beginning to end.

141.subject: Budgets
141.title: Part III - Adding a Task
141.text: Getting started.. Adding Tasks To get started building a budget, you can start by setting the contingency amounts. To do this, click the 'Budget Settings' button in the 'Overall Project Budget' section.For this example, we’ve set both the soft cost contingency and hard cost contingency to $25,000 each. Setting contingency is of course part of the budget, so after setting these both to $25,000, our overall project budget summary is showing we have an original pre-close budget of $50,000. Now for the fun part. Building the budget. TasksIn order to build out the budget, a user now adds one line item at a time of the budget using the ‘Add Task’ button. Task Name: When adding a task, a user must give the task a name, such as ‘Architect,’ they then choose a category. Categories are: OtherIncomeFinanceConstructionCommissions / Leasing FeesYou (or an administrator with Lists & Tools access) can add additional budget task categories from the Lists and Tools section > Budget Task categories.Company: you can also choose a company from the directory to associate the task / line item to. Cost Type: now choose between soft cost and hard cost type. Original Pre Close Budget: this is the amount of the budget being allocated to this task / line item. Notes: simply a spot to leave notes regarding the task / line item. You can also choose to add an attachment to your task.When finished, click ‘Add Task’ a new line item will appear in either the soft cost budget or the hard cost budget section. The total will also get aggregated in the top overall budget section. Here, I’ve added a task / line item of architect and allocated $25,000 of my budget for this purpose. Notice how my hard cost totals have now gone from $25,000 to $50,000 and my overall totals have now gone from $50,000 to $75,000. The next step is to repeat the past few steps and add line items for each new task needed. For the purpose of this example, and also for the sake of simplicity, I’ve made my budget comprised of two soft costs tasks ($25,000) as well as two hard cost tasks ($25,000). This brings my total soft costs to $75,000, my total hard costs to $75,000, and my overall total to $150,000. Now we have a very basic original pre close budget. If we need to edit the details of the budget cost, you can do so by clicking the pencil icon that appears when hovering over the cost.

142.subject: Budgets
142.title: Part IV - Adjusting, Sending for Approval, & Locking
142.text: Adjusting, Sending for Approval, & LockingTo adjust, send for approval, or lock a change order you'd click thebutton.From here, since the original pre close budget has not been approved / locked yet. A user can simply type in new values for these different tasks / line items. The changes are automatically saved.Once the original Pre Close Budget is finished being set up, it’s now ready for approval. Close this window.Click the button in the top right.The request approval window should be familiar to you, as its fields are exactly the same as approval requests on file overviews. Essentially, what you’re going to do is send this to someone at your company who is designated as the budget approver, typically the CEO. That should be the only person with permissions to approve a budget. One difference with the budget approval request window, from other approval requests in DealforceCRE, is that you must choose which budget you’re requesting approval for: Original pre close budgetCurrent pre close budgetOriginal post close budgetFor my example, I’ll be using the original pre close budget, since that’s all we have built up to this point. Click send for approval. The budget approver will see the familiar Approve / Reject buttons.If rejected, the system will prompt the user to leave comments, which can be done by clicking on the actions button and choosing the ‘budget history and comments’ option: For now, let’s hit approve. In the top right ‘budget approvals’ section we can now see the original pre close budget was approved. Now that the budget has been approved, the same person approving the budget, can click on the ‘Adjust Budget’ button, and from here, they can now lock the original pre-close budget. To do so, they would click the ‘locked’ checkbox just below the ‘original pre close budget’ title. Doing so will lock these line items so that the original pre close budget can no longer be adjusted, as well as copy over all the values from the line items in the original pre close budget column, to the current pre close budget column, which now unlocks. They should then click save.

143.subject: Budgets
143.title: Part V - Current Pre-Close, Post-Close Budget
143.text: Current Pre-Close, Post-Close BudgetNow as the actual work begins on the project, users will come in here to adjust each line item as variances occur.Let’s say that our taxes turned out to be $30,000 instead of the projected $25,000. A user would now come into the system, and adjust the numbers manually. Notice, however, when we change the $25,000 to $30,000 for legal fees, we are now showing near the totals at the bottom that we are $5,000 over budget. That is because, when a line item is increased, the user needs to make sure to then manually reduce the same exact amount from the corresponding contingency balance. Since legal fees is a soft cost, a user would now subtract $5000 from the soft cost budget, and apply that $5,000 to the legal fees line item. Notice that when I subtract $5,000 from soft cost contingency, and add it to legal fees, the bottom totals show ‘balanced.’ The goal of the person adjusting the budget is to try and balance when possible, this will include the likelihood that the current pre close budget gets approved. Had the legal fees only been $20,000 instead of $25,000, the user could have just reduced legal fees by $5,000 and not had to touch the contingency balance. This would have caused the totals at the bottom to appear: $5,000.00 Under BudgetOnce the contingency balance has been depleted, if users need to increase other line items, users have no choice but to have a budget that is ‘over budget.’Once the current Pre-close budget is finished being prepared, it can now be sent for approval. Again, click the ‘send for approval’ button / link in the top right. Follow the same prompts as explained earlier when requesting approval, only this time, the user would request approval for the ‘current pre close budget.’ Let’s say the approver then goes in and approves the current pre close budget. Now our budget approvals would show as: At this point, the approver needs to remember to go into the ‘adjust budget window,’ and lock the current pre close budget. Doing so will again move over all the values from the ‘current pre close budget’ column to the ‘original post close budget column’ which will then become unlocked. The approve would hit save. Then, after the closing of the project, users could come in and make any final adjustments based upon all final financial figures in the original post close budget. Once done, the approval process occurs again, the approver could then approve the final Original Post Close Budget. Here’s an example of a budget that has been 100% approved at all phases. And finally, the approver could then go in and lock the final original post close budget. Here’s an example of a completed budget: In this simple example. The contingency was not needed in the end, therefore it was deduced from the budget, and the project came in $45,000 under budget. Now the organization can see the variance between the original pre close budget, the current pre close budget, and the original post close budget. The differences between these columns will assist in making better financial projects, determining problem areas, as well as provide many other insights.

144.subject: Budgets
144.title: Part VI - Import & Export
144.text: Extra Tools!There are a few helpful tools available to the user to make this process more streamlined. These tools are found in the ‘Actions’ dropdown. Here, we have three different options: Budget History and CommentsDownloadImport Budget TasksBudget Task CategoriesLet’s finish this training off by dissecting each of these. Budget History and CommentsA window to see a breakdown of budget approvals / budget history / and comments DownloadYou can download the budget to CSV, or in a PDF format. This allows users to export each task / line item to an excel file (CSV), which can then presumably be pasted into a pro forma worksheet. The PDF export exactly mirrors the budget appearance in DealforceCRE. Import Budget TasksUnderstandably, it could become very time consuming to create each individual task / line item on every single project. Because of this fact, users will have the ability to import a budget from one project to the next. This works similarly to how importing a schedule template works. Simply go to the new project to which you’d like to import a budget for, click the ‘import budget tasks’ button. From here you choose the project / budget you want to pull in. And then choose whether you’d like to pull in soft costs, hard costs, or both. Click ‘import’ to finish the import. All of the tasks / line items from that project will pull in. This of course means you don’t need to re-create every single task / line item on each project, you have to enter in proper values for each line item. Budget Task CategoriesThis option allows the user to reorder the task categories and add additional categories, if needed.

145.subject: Finance Tab
145.title: Finance Page Overview
145.text: Along with many other department tabs, the Finance tab in DealforceCRE is a specific section of the application intended exclusively for tracking all of the financial details relating to a project. To get started, head to a project and click on the 'Finance' tab . The exact placement for the tab differs from user to user. If you cannot find the Finance tab at the top, click 'All Tabs' and locate it in the dropdown list.The finance tab is used for adding all purchase details across an entire project and like many other pages in DealforceCRE, the page is broken down into three main sectionsDefault fields Custom fields Todos General info, 'Partner' details, 'Bridge Lender' details, loan info, etc are all default fields that can be recorded on the finance tabSimilar to many other tabs within DealforceCRE, todos may be added either individually on the finance tabOr a list of todos can be imported, by clicking 'Actions' *Global todos may be created under 'Lists & Tools' > 'Todos' > 'Finance Todos'

146.subject: Finance Tab
146.title: Partner/Lender & Loan Info
146.text: Users have the ability to list the information for multiple partners on the finance tab. By default, fields for one partner will be displayed. Additional partners can be added by clicking the Add Partner link. Each partner addition will include fields for Partner, Partner’s Equity, and % Interest.Users can select the appropriate partner contact from the list of contacts found in the directoryThe following section of default fields is used for storing bridge lender dataIt is worth nothing that the finance page features numerous date fields, which create a schedule item when a date is inputted. Some examples include the 'Bridge Lender Earliest Payoff Date' , 'Bridge Lender Paid Off' , 'Primary Lender' fields, etc. Clicking 'Add' opens up the same schedule item popup found on the project's schedule tabA schedule item date may be entered here for 'Projected Sale Date'If we head to the 'Schedule' tab for the project, we can now see the schedule item entered on the finance tab

147.subject: Finance Tab
147.title: Finance Tab Customization
147.text: As with many features within DealforceCRE, the finance tab may be a modified to display preferred placement for todos, custom fields and default fields. The default layout is default fields at the top left portion of the page, custom fields beneath default fields and todos on the left. The order for these features may be modified within 'Lists & Tools' > 'Categories & Lists' > 'Customize Tabs' > 'Finance' The placement order is changed by dragging and dropping the stack icon for the desired section, over to the location on the page where the user would like to relocate the feature. Additionally, the default fields shown below may be displayed/hidden from the finance page as needed.

148.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
148.title: Intro to Box
148.text: Box and Box Drive are fully integrated with DealforceCRE.The following information covers Box Drive installation on your computer. In addition, there is also a video covering how Box works with DealforceCRE, linked at the bottom of this email. You should have received an email from Box.com confirming that you have been added as a new user (please check spam/junk/trash if not delivered to your inbox).To download Box Drive, follow these instructions:1. Click here to visit the Box Drive download page. 2. Select whether you have a Windows or Mac computer. Note that you'll need at least Windows 7 in order to run Box Drive3. Download the file and run the installer4. Once installed, you'll be asked to use your login credentials.
