You will now see Box in your File ExplorerAnd here is a quick instructional video showing how box drive works with DealForceCRE. Box Drive - Watch Video

149.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
149.title: Intro to Dealforce File Management
149.text: As mentioned in the previous topic, Box Drive is integrated into DealforceCRE.Below, you'll see files and their corresponding file directories. They way that they're laid out in Dealforce is exactly as it is in Box. This is because Dealforce is pulling all of its file structures for projects, paperwork, etc from Box.This is extremely convenient. However, it also means whatever you add or remove from Box will be removed from Dealforce. The opposite is true: if you delete something from Dealforce, it's gone from Box as well. Be entirely sure of what you're deleting!

150.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
150.title: Creating / Editing Files & Folders - Box
150.text: Box and Dealforce are fully integrated. What this means is: if you create or delete a file or folder in Box or Box Drive, the same action will occur within the 'Files' area of Dealforce. The opposite is true as well. In the example below, examples are shown of how to work within the desktop Box program.To manage files within Box Drive, first open the desktop app:NOTE: If you do not have this application on your Mac or PC, you can download it from here.Once you're signed into the Box Drive, you should be presented with a file structure somewhere along the lines of this:From here, you'll decide where you'd like to create a a folder. For this example, let's say you're creating a file within an already existing project. Let's call the new folder 'PHOTOS'.The creation of a file within Box is the same as any other part of Mac or Windows-- Simply: Right Click > New Folder > Name Folder.Once the folder is created, you can now add files to it. Let's add a picture to it. Simply drag and drop any file (in this case a .jpg photo) into the folder you've created.Deleting these files and folders is just as easy as adding them. Simply highlight the folder or file that you want to delete, and press 'Command + Delete', or in windows just the 'delete key'. You can also drag the file/folder to your trash can. You'll be prompted to confirm you're sure that you're trying to delete the correct folder or file.In the next topic, we'll demonstrate what this Box file system looks like within Dealforce. Creating and editing files within Dealforce will also be covered.

151.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
151.title: Creating / Editing Files & Folders - Dealforce
151.text: Within Dealforce, there are a few different ways that you can view files. One way is from a global view. From the global bar, select 'Files', and then one of the corresponding options. Below explains what each of these options do: Files: Shows the global Company Files Tree. This is basically departmental files where various department employees store their informationAt the bottom of this page, there's a file called 'My Files', where users can store more personal files.Approvals: Shows the files that have been sent for approval in Dealforce.Signatures: Shows the files that have been sent for signature in Dealforce.Verifications: Shows the files that have been sent for verifications in Dealforce.NOTE: Approval, Signature, and Verification files can filtered within their respective pages.Another way to access files in Dealforce (and how this example will be shown) is through projects. Let's check out how the file that was added in Box reflects in Dealforce. First, navigate to the project in which the file was created.You'll be presented with a screen similar to the one below (depending on which files you have within the project).Let's look for the folder we created earlier:There it is! Let's click into it and see what's inside.As you can see, the photo that we'd originally placed in the Box created file reflects within Dealforce. There are also more options for this folder, including:Upload FilesUpload FolderCreate FolderPreviewDownloadUpload New VersionShareEditLet's click on the photo and see how it appears:From this screen, you can request approval or signature for the file, as well as additional options within the 'actions' drop down. You also have the ability to leave comments for all users, or just internal. Tags, adding to Todo's, adding to key documents, and other options are available as well.To delete an item from the Dealforce file manager, click the pencil icon next to the file and click delete. This will also delete the file from Box. The same process applies to folders in Dealforce.

152.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
152.title: Sharing a File / Folder in Box & Dealforce
152.text: To share a file or folder in Box:Right click the file or folder that you would like to share. Hover over 'share' to bring up the share menu.Here you have the option to share, email, or manage the collaborators with the file or folder.To share a file or folder in Dealforce:Click the arrow button as shown below to bring up the share option for either a file or folder within Dealforce.The below share modal will appear, with a variety of options that you can utilize to share the file or folder.

153.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
153.title: Setting up G-Suite & Office 365 in Dealforce & Box
153.text: Looking for a faster way to edit files in DealforceCRE? Our G-Suite / Office 365 integrations make it possible to edit files from the file overview page in DF, so you no longer have to download a file, edit and re-upload the file in most cases. First, a few quick configuration steps are required. Log into your Box.com account and enable the integration(s). In Box.com, click on your initials / profile image in the top right corner, and click on the ‘Account Settings’ option. Next, click on the ‘integrations’ tab to the right and check the ‘Enable Box for G Suite’ box, if you are using G-Suite, or Office Online if you are using Office. Next, you will need to enable in DealforceCRE. Click on your name at the top-right portion of the page, then click account. Scroll down your account settings to the 'Linked Third Party Apps' section. Ensure all of the below boxes are checked: The configuration steps are now complete. Now you can edit files in Dealforce with these integrations. Locate a file, click ‘Actions’ on the file overview page and choose the application in which to open the file Once you’ve completed your edits to the file, simply close out of the MS/G-Suite tab and your edits will automatically save in DF, without having to download and re-upload the file.*Important note: your G-Mail/365 address must be the same as their box email address. Example, a user’s email associated to G Suite is support@dealforcecre.com, then the users box account must also be this same exact email address.*

154.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
154.title: Using Office 365 and G-Suite Integration in DealforceCRE
154.text: Once you have set up the Office 365 and G-Suite integrations, you are now able to utilize these features. They all live within areas that store files. When viewing a file, you can click on the "Actions" button at the top right of the screen to bring up the below menu. The Office and G-Suite integrations are highlighted:You can collaborate with any users that have access to DealforceCRE on these documents automatically, by clicking on either of the above options. When the "Open MS Word" button is pressed, you'll be presented with a screen like the one below. You can edit this document using all of the Microsoft Word online features. Once you are finished, simply closing the tab will save your work. It is already saving your changes automatically to Box, and DealforceCRE. When the "Open in Google Docs" button is pressed, it will open up a window similar to that of Microsoft Word, except you will be able to edit the document in Google Docs. Just like the Word integration, your changes are being saved real-time to both Box and DealforceCRE.Note: It may take up to a minute for your document changes to appear in DealforceCRE.

155.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
155.title: Use @mentions in comments
155.text: Pro Tip: It's important to continue to use the @mentions to keep all the necessary parties in the loop! Otherwise, communication and information can be dropped.1. When leaving a comment in DealforceCRE, you can tag users by first typing the '@' icon, and then their name. This will populate a list of users that you can select from. This applies in all comment fields throughout DealforceCRE. 2. When a user mentions you in a comment, you'll receive a notification based on your selected notification preference.3. Once you click the notification, you'll be taken to the comment where you can then respond by clicking the 'Reply' button. This will automatically add the user's handle (@username) to the comment field.

156.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
156.title: Request approval of files internally
156.text: 1. To request approval of a file from an internal user, click the Request Approval button in the top right hand corner of the file preview. 2. Enter the name of the internal users you would like to have review and either approve or reject the file. You can set an approving order, which means that the approvals are sent out in the order listed. If the first person rejects the file, it does not go onto the second person in this case.3. Set a due date, which will prompt reminders for the requested users. 4. Click Send for Approval and you're all set! The recipients will now receive notifications based on their selected settings regarding your request to approve the file.5. Once you've sent a request for Approval, the activity will show in the File History where you can also send push notification reminders to the recipients.

157.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
157.title: Approve or reject a file
157.text: 1. When your approval is requested on a file, you will receive a notification either by in-app notification, email notification or Daily Digest depending on your settings. We highly recommend keeping these notifications in-app to ensure quick response time.2. When you click on the notification, it will take you to the file overview with Approve and Reject buttons at the top of the file view. 3. Click Approve if there are not any changes or updates that need to be made to the file.4. If you reject a file, there is a prompt to leave a comment with any feedback (tagging the requestor) so they can make the necessary updates to the file before submitting again.

158.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
158.title: View approvals overview
158.text: 1. Click Files and then Approvals in the left menu navigation.2. Filter the requests based on Project Name, Recipients, Requestor, Status, etc. and then click on the File Name to view the file details.

159.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
159.title: Archiving an approval request
159.text: Archiving an approval request is a Super Admin function, therefore only a few users have this ability. If you require an approval request to be archived, please reach out to an appropriate user.________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________Approval requests that have not been approved or denied yet can be canceled/archived from the Approvals section within the Global Directory.From here, hover over any request that is not completed or archived. Sent is eligible to be archived. The icon would look like a small box, like this:When you click it, simply confirm that you'd like to archive the approval request.

160.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
160.title: Request signature from internal or external user
160.text: 1. Once you've navigated to your file view, click the Request Signature button at the top of the view.2. As with the file approval process, you will be able to enter the Signer's name, which will populate a set of internal users and complete the email field. This is true for both internal and external signers.4. As with approvals, you can add additional signers by clicking Add Recipient and then set the signing order by clicking the Set Signing Order button and then adding the correlating order of signing.5. Add a Subject, which will be the subject of the email that the user receives when they receive the request and an optional message and then click Prepare for Signing. Each request, no matter how many signers, costs $2, so it's important to make sure you've added all the correct parties.6. Once you click Prepare for Signing, you'll be taken to the DocuSign window where you can drag and drop fields onto the document. As you can see from the below screenshot, the signature and name field were drag and dropped onto the document.

161.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
161.title: Request a wet signature
161.text: 1. Once you click the Request Signature button, if you click the Print & Sign button instead of the Prepare for Signature button, and the file will then download to your desktop for you to deliver it to the in-person signing parties. This solution saves the company the $2 envelope costs, so be sure to click the right one for these instances.2. Once the file has been signed, the process is completed by clicking the Complete Wet Signature button in the File History and uploading the signed version.

162.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
162.title: Complete a signature request
162.text: 1. When a signature is requested, the user will receive a notification based on their notification preferences, either in-app, email or Daily Digest. When the user clicks on the notification, they'll be taken to the file where they'll see the DocuSign signing window.We recommend keeping signature request notifications on in-app to ensure quick turn-around! 2. Another way to access existing signature requests is by clicking on Files and Signatures in the left navigation and clicking on the blue icon on the right hand side of the list. 3. Read the prompts and then scroll to find where your signature and any other fields is being requested. Click the boxes and it will populate a signing window where you can adopt a signature or sign on your own. 4. When you're done, click Finish. You will receive a signed version of the file once all parties have signed.

163.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
163.title: Deny a signature request
163.text: 1. If your signature is requested and you do not want to sign the file, click into the request and click the top right hand button that says Other Actions and then Decline to Sign. This will send a notification to the requestor that you have denied signing the file.2. Once you have denied the file, navigate back to the file overview and leave a comment on the right hand side, tagging the requestor, explaining why you denied the file.

164.subject: Box & Dealforce File Management, Approvals, Signatures
164.title: Archiving a signature request
164.text: Archiving a signature request is a Super Admin function, therefore only a few users have this ability. If you require a signature request to be archived, please reach out to an appropriate user.________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________Signature requests that have not been completed yet can be canceled/archived from the Signatures section within the Global Directory.From here, hover over any request that is not completed or archived. Sent and Delivered are eligible to be archived. The icon would look like a small box, like this:When you click it, simply confirm that you'd like to archive the signature request.

165.subject: External Users
165.title: Inviting External Users
165.text: Allowing external users to access Dealforce can be a very helpful tool. By logging into the system, these users can view specific information about the projects that they are involved with as well as perform tasks like entering bids, requesting payments, and submitting change orders.The first step to inviting an external user is to add them as a contact in DealforceCRE. This can be accomplished in multiple ways. The most basic way is to add them as a Contact through the Directory from the global menu on the left.Click Add Contact and then fill in the fields. Contact Name is the only required field, but we recommend filling in all available information. Keep in mind, while they are not required fields, adding a company name and an email address is necessary in order to invite the contact to register for DealforceCRE.Contacts can also be added from within various areas of DealforceCRE. One example is through the Project level Contacts tab. After clicking Add Contact from this tab, select the +New Contact button. New contacts can also be added from the Purchase and Sales tabs by clicking Add Seller or Add Buyer and then the +New Contact button.The advantage of adding the new contact via the Project level Contacts, Purchase, or Sales tab is that the contact will automatically be linked to the project and show in the Contacts tab. If the contact is added from the Directory, they will still need to be added to the Contacts tab within the Project.Once the contact is listed on the Contacts tab within the Project, they can be invited to create a DealforceCRE login.To do this, select the Contact Name, click permissions, and then click the toggle within the App Access section.In the Grant App Access screen, fill in the email address and company name (if not already present). If external user roles have been set up, choose the role that includes the permissions you would like the user to have. We will go over permissions in more detail in the next section.In the bottom section, choose the project(s) that you would like the user to have access to, and set their permissions for payment requests, refunds, and comments. Click Grant App Access.Once access has been granted, the App Access area will look a little different and will include a "Pending Invitation" badge. This will remain until the external user sets up their account by clicking on the email they received. If the invitation email needs to be resent, click the envelope icon to the right.Permissions for this user can be modified at any time by clicking the pencil icon next to 'App Access'. From here, users can select another role to copy permissions from, or another user's permissions to mirror.Admins in DealforceCRE also have access to adjust permissions manually, aside from using roles or mirroring users and the 'Global Permissions' is another permissions option that they can edit with the same pencil icon. Admins have access to modify individual permissions for each feature in the app, which can be toggled on and off in this setting area:For help with updating roles, please reach out to your DealforceCRE admin. It's important to note that system admins also have access to "impersonate" user accounts, meaning the ability to log into user accounts while masquerading their profile. This is helpful when confirmation might be needed that specific features are accessible to other users, or that permissions are not being overextended to external users for features in the application which they should not have access to.

166.subject: External Users
166.topic: Setting Up Permissions for External Users
166.title: Setting Up Permissions for External Users
166.text: Aside from the permissions that are listed in the App Access area of the contact, Dealforce gives you the ability to create roles that can be assigned to external users that include a standard set of permissions. These are typically created based on the type of user and dictate what areas of the app that type of user is able to access.These roles must be set up by someone that has administrator access within the software, but the roles can be assigned by anyone that has access to add external users.To create an external user role, click your name in the top right corner, then click 'Users'. Finally, click on 'Roles'Now click the Add Role button. In the Add Role window, give the role a name. This is typically going to be the user type such as Bidder, Contractor, etc. Next, set the radio button to External User. Then, you will need to make selections for this type of user based on what permissions you would like them to have access to. There is a section for Global Permissions and one for Project Permissions. All permissions have options available for No Access and Read/Write abilities. Some also have a Read Only option. Once all selections have been made, click Save.Now, when a new external user is being given app access, this new role can be chosen from the Grant Permissions dropdown. This user will have access to only the areas that are set for this user role.

167.subject: External Users
167.topic: Using DealforceCRE as an External User
167.title: Using DealforceCRE as an External User
167.text: When an external user is invited to create a DealforceCRE account, they will receive an email like this:The user will click on the Accept Invitation button and the following screen will open in their web browser. They will need to verify that their name and email address are correct and then create a password. Once all fields are populated, click Set My Password.Once the external user has set up their credentials, they will be able to log into the system. They will access the app through the same web address that an internal user would use. While the external user will only be able to access those projects they are assigned to and will only be able to see those areas that their permissions allow, the navigation through the site will be the same as an internal user.

168.subject: Reports
168.title: Reports in DealforceCRE
168.text: DealforceCRE is an extremely 'Data Heavy' application. That is to say, there are hundreds of fields and data points captured throughout the application. The more data is populated in a company's instance of DealforceCRE, the more useful the reporting features in DealforceCRE become. DealforceCRE has a dedicated report builder, which we will cover in this module, but that's not the only area where one can view a report. Therefore, when someone says 'Run a Report,' they might not always be talking about a report created with the report builder. It's important to know what a report is in DealforceCRE. Definition: A report in DealforceCRE is any area throughout the application where qualitative and / or quantitative data can be queried for informative purposes. Usually, this data can be sorted, and / or filtered, and / or downloaded. Reports are found in three primary areas: 1). Under the 'Reports' link in the global navigation: 2). In the Global areas 3). On project specific Indices In this module, we will cover all of these areas.

169.subject: Reports
169.title: Default Reports
169.text: Every instance of DealforceCRE includes a standard set of default reports. These can be found by clicking on Reports in the global menu on the left. All reports that are listed above Report Builder are stock reports and cannot be changed.Clicking on the title of any of these reports will bring it up for viewing on your screen. Once the report is on your screen, you can choose to filter the results if needed. You can also click on the column headers to adjust the sorting. After making any necessary alterations, clicking the Download button in the upper right will download a copy of what is shown on the screen in .csv format.In addition to the filters within a report, you can also scroll all the way to the right of the report. There, you'll find a icon. If you click this, you'll receive the option to choose which headings you'd like to appear within the report:

170.subject: Reports
170.title: Report Builder
170.text: Report Builder is a tool where users can create custom reports comprised of data pulled from any combination of fields throughout DealforceCRE. Begin by clicking Report Builder, nested within Reports, from within the Reports Global Menu.On the Report Builder screen, the first step is to give your new report a name. Make sure the name is unique and that it accurately describes the contents of the report. This will help to locate the correct report when you are ready to run it in the future.After selecting a title, you have the option of making your report available to other users. If you would like others to be able to run this report, check the Share Template checkbox. If you do not check this box, you will be the only person who sees the report in the list.A note on sharing reports - while all internal users will be able to run all shared reports, only information the user has access to based on their permissions will display on the reports.We are now ready to add fields to our report. By default, the Project name field is always the first column on reports created through Report Builder, so it does not need to be added.You have two options for how to add additional fields. The first option is to navigate through the various categories by clicking the arrow, and then clicking the plus sign next to the fields you would like to add. This option makes the most sense if you aren't really sure what all of the columns are that you want to add. This method allows you to go through each category and choose the pertinent fields.However, if you already know what you want in your report, the search option may be a better approach. When using the search, as you type, the available field list will adjust to only display the results that include the text entered in the search field. As with the previous method, click the plus sign to add it to the report. To add additional fields through this method, delete the search parameter and enter the next field you would like to add.Once all fields have been added to the list on the right, check to make sure they are in the desired order for the report. If they need to be reordered, click and hold on the 3 lines to the left of the field name that needs to be moved and drag it up or down to where it should be. Now that all of the fields are in place, click Save to complete the report. The results of the report will now display on the screen.If any additional adjustments need to be made, click the Edit Report button at the top of the screen to go back to the Report Builder screen.Once the report has been saved, it will show in the Global Menu to the left below Templates. Each user will be able to access reports that they created from here.Here is an example of what a final report looks like when viewing it: Please know that anywhere where there is missing data (such as when the report says 'edit' or 'add' like in the example above), clicking right on the edit / add link will allow the user to input data directly into the report. Finally, there are a few other useful tools on this report view on the top right. Save Changes: Click this after filtering or sorting data to save the filtered/sorted version.Edit Report : Allows the user to edit the fields in the report. Download: Downloads the report to CSV format. Duplicate: The duplicate icon simply allows users to make a copy of the report, in case they want to create a new report, but want to use the current report as a starting place.

171.subject: Reports
171.title: Templates
171.text: If the Share Template box was checked when the report was created through Report Builder, it will also be listed within Templates along with any shared reports created by other users within the organization.To run the report, click on the name. Filtering and sorting options are available as they are with stock reports. The Download option is also available.

172.subject: Reports
172.title: Global Reports
172.text: If you're looking for a report or section based on a specific thing such as schedule, todo's, or bids, click the icon within the global navigation bar.For instance, if a report is needed on all projects, click on the global projects. From here the data can be filtered and sorted. A few of the key filters in the global projects page are: Project Status, Project Developer, and Project Role. Each global page works similarly in that they each of key filters that are relevant to that data: Schedule Items: Key date type, date rangeTodos: Assignee, followers, todo list Comments: Project, SenderPayments: Contract name, payee, etc.Bids: Bid contact, date rangeWorkspaces: User accessThese are thought of as reports as well because data can be viewed and organized and some are available for download as well.

173.subject: Reports
173.title: Project Specific Indices
173.text: As with global reports, there are also project specific reports that can be created and / or downloaded from various tabs within the project. These include a few of the same types such as Schedule Items and Payments. There are also a few formatted reports that can be downloaded:Lease Abstract - downloaded from the Tenant Page under the Lease/Mgmt tab (suites must be present with tenants assigned in order to produce a Lease Abstract).SIR Report - downloaded by clicking the Print PDF button from within the SIR tab. The report generated will include all sections within the SIR.This is not an exhaustive list of all the project specific indices, but rather, a small sample of the different areas that could be considered reports. Remember, anywhere that data can be sorted, filtered and / or downloaded, it can be considered a report.

174.subject: Admin Modules
174.title: Adding a New Internal User
174.text: To add a new internal user, go to Admin Settings > Users from the top navigation bar.On the Users screen, click the button. You will need to fill in the First and Last Name and Email Address for the new user. Make selections in the radio buttons based on the permissions this user should have. Click Next.On the Permissions tab, make selections for each line based on what is necessary for this user to be able to perform their job duties. No Access will prevent them from seeing anything in that area.Read Only will allow them to see the area, but not make any changes.Read/Write will allow them full rights to view and make changes. Once complete, click Done. Please note that the top section of the permissions labeled "Global Permissions" relates to the global navigation which is located at all times the navigation bar in the left of the screen.Also note, the section below labeled 'Project Permissions' relates to the specific tabs within a project. For instance, if a user had no permissions other than just Read / Write permissions on the construction tab, when that user logged in and clicked on a project, they would only see the construction tab, and no other areas. The new user will now receive the following Invitation Instructions via email to set up their account.Hello <<New User>>,<<Admin User>> has invited you to you can accept it through the link below.Accept Invitation (clickable link)This invitation will expire on <<5 days from today's date>>. If you don't want to accept the invitation, please ignore this email. Your account won't be created until you access the link above and set your password.Thanks, Your Team at <<Company Name>>Clicking on the link will allow the user to set up their account and create a password.User RolesWhen creating a new user, you may notice that there are a lot of available options on the Permissions tab. Fortunately, there is a way to make setting these up a little easier than individually choosing each permission setting upon the creation of the new user. DealforceCRE gives you the ability to save User Roles.This is very helpful if you have multiple employees that have the same (or very similar) permissions. This way, you don't have to think about what their permissions are allowing them to see / not see, you can simply assign them a pre-defined role, and rest assured that their permissions will be appropriate. There are two ways to set up a User Role. First, click on Admin Settings > Users and then select the Roles tab. Click on the Add Role button.In the Add Role screen, give the role a name and then make all of the necessary selections for someone that is assigned to that role. When you are done, click Save.Then, when you are setting up your user, just select the new role you created from the Select Existing Role dropdown on the Permissions tab within the Add User screen, and all of the proper permission settings will adjust accordingly. Now click save, and the user will be given the permissions associated to that role. The other way to create a user role is from this same Permissions tab. Go ahead and make the selections below for the permissions you want that employee to have. Let's say you are setting up a new user to have special finance permissions (process and approve payments, adjust and unlock the budget). If you imagine that this role might be useful for future users, you can actually create the role at the same time that you are giving the individual user that set of permissions. For this example, you would set the proper settings, and then type the word 'finance' into the 'Enter new role name' box in the top right, and then hit done. The user will be created with the appropriate permissions. The new 'finance' role will be created also, for future use.

175.subject: Admin Modules
175.title: Lists & Tools
175.text: The Lists & Tools area is where you can set up various lists of values that your application will pull from. As the name implies, this area also offers a handfull of handy tools that can be used on all projects. The List & Tools section can be found under the Admin Settings menu item at the top of the screen next to your name. This area is only available to those with admin permissions.**Note: If you need something adjusted in this section, either ask your administrator for this permission, or ask the admin to make the changes for you**The options available within the Lists & Tools screen are separated into four groups: Categories/ListsTodosCustom TodosTemplatesToolsClick the arrow next to a group to expand the list. Categories/Lists includes various lists and values you can define, which can then be used throughout the app.Todos is where you will set up standard todos that populate every time a new project is added.Custom Todos is where you can add lists of custom todos.Templates is where you set up bid sheet and lien waiver templates.Tools currently houses the Checklist Builder.

176.subject: Admin Modules
176.title: Categories / Lists
176.text: The Categories / Lists section is where you can define the values from various fields within the application. We will go over a few of the more commonly used options here.DepartmentsFirst, let's look at Departments. Entering departments into the departments list in List & Tools allows those departments / values entered to then be associated to internal users. Once the departments are created, users are then associated to specific departments for organization and reporting purposes. Key Date TypesNext, we'll go over Key Date Types. These are used for identifying common or key schedule items. By default, there is a list of Key Dates already in the system. Some of the default key dates in the system include: Estimated Purchase DateGC BidsLease Delivery (and many more) Additional items can be added by clicking the Add Key Date Type button in the upper right.The purpose of these key dates is to be able to choose them when creating schedule items, so that the schedule items do not need to be completed from scratch every time. A Key Date can be added to the schedule by going to the Schedule tab within a project, clicking the Add to Schedule button, checking the Key Date box, and then choosing one from Key Date Type dropdown. The values that appear in the Key Date Type dropdown will be those default Key Dates in the system, as well as any other custom Key Date types have been entered in the List & Tools section. Custom FieldsCustom Fields can be added at the bottom of most tabs within each project. You may, however, find yourself adding the same custom fields to every new project. In this situation, you should add these fields in the Custom Fields section of Lists & Tools. Adding a custom field here makes that field an automatic addition to every project, both current and new. To add the custom field, first select the tab you want it to appear on from the Select Project Tab dropdown.Once you have selected the tab, click the Add Custom Field button. In the screen that comes up, enter a Field Name and select the Field Type from the dropdown. Options here include Short Text, Date, Link to File, and numerous others.Once you save the new custom field, the field will exist on the designated tab for all projects. Project RolesThe last item we will cover in this section is Project Roles. These are incredibly useful because they allow you to set specific users to these roles for each project. In doing this, you now have the ability to set a Project Role as a default assignee or follower on schedule items or todos. When users are associated to the various roles for a project, they would automatically begin getting notifications for any of these items linked to their role.To set up Project Roles, click the Add Project Role button from within this section of Categories/Lists. Fill in the name of the role and Save.Some common Project Roles may include: Project ManagerDirector of ConstructionDeveloper

177.subject: Admin Modules
177.title: Todos
177.text: Todos are essentially reminders of things you and your colleagues need 'todo.' These todos can be found on many of the project tabs. While it is very possible that you may have numerous one-off items, you probably also have a standard list of todos for various tabs within each project. Example: You might have a common marketing todos that occur on every projectPrepare marketing flyerPrepare offering memorandumFor these, it is much more beneficial to add the todos on a global level. Doing so means that on each new project that is added, this pre-defined list of todos will be pulled in. To begin, go to the Todos section in the Lists & Tools area. Here, you will see a long list of all of the different types of Todos available. Click on the list to which you'd like to add a todo. Once you have selected the proper Todo list, click the corresponding 'Add' button in the upper right.In the screen that comes up, create a title for your Todo. Also, while not required, you may want to choose Assignees and Followers. This can be a huge time saver if you are using Project Roles. You can choose a Project Role to assign the Todo to. Then, when a project is created and the users are associated to project roles, those users will effectively be assigned those todos via their role. If you would like to use these todos on any pre-existing projects, go to the corresponding tab for the project, click the Actions dropdown, and choose Import Todos. If the Actions dropdown is not shown, then there aren't any available todos for that tab.

178.subject: Admin Modules
178.title: Templates
178.text: The Templates section currently houses Bid Sheet and Lien Waiver templates as well as the Template Builder. The details of the Template Builder are included in another section. To create a Bid Sheet Template, first click the Add button in the upper right.Give the template a name and then click Add Section to begin adding the fields that your bidders will populate.Hovering over a line item will bring up two icons to the left. The icon with the three lines is for sorting. You can click and hold on this icon and then drag to reorder your list.Clicking on the arrow icon activates the ability to add Subsections to that Section.Click Save Template when complete. This template is now available for use when inviting bidders to bid on a package.Lien Waiver Templates can also be loaded into DealforceCRE for use when making payments against contracts. Custom Lien Waiver templates can be quite complex, therefore, if your organization chooses to use these, please contact us at support@dealforcecre.freshdesk.com or submit a ticket from the Help menu.

179.subject: Admin Modules
179.title: Tools
179.text: Currently, the only item available in the Tools area is the Checklist Builder. Additional items will be added to this section in the future.Checklist BuilderBefore we jump into how to create a checklist, let's talk about the philosophy behind what these are. Checklists are actually somewhat similar to 'todos' but they are different in a few important ways. Todos are perfect for informal reminders of pieces of work that needs to be completed. Todos can have assignees and followers. Todos are independent from each other, generally speaking. When creating a todo list of 3 items, these todos do not have to have anything to do with one another. This is where checklists are different. Checklists are also for reminders of bits of work that needs to get done, or for things that need to be checked off / authorized. The big difference here, is that the Checklist Builder allows you to create a sequence of things that need to be completed. For example, let's say you have a checklist of ten things that must be confirmed before a contract is signed, this is when a checklist is best. Let's say these three items are: Verify accurate contract amountsVerify accurate datesVerify proper contract termsThis is an over simplified example of a checklist, but the point of this is, 100% of these things need to get checked off before some action occurs (such as signing a contract). General rule of thumb for Todos: use todos instead of a checklist when you have a date related to the item, you have assignees or followers who should be associated to the work, or when the items are not necessarily part of a sequence. General rule of thumb for Checklist: use a checklist instead of todos when the items relate to a document, or when you need verify a sequence of things before another action can occur.To create your own custom checklist, select Checklist Builder from within the Tools area and then click on Add Checklist.Give the checklist a name and choose a type. Name: A generic name to identify what the checklist does (Example: PSA Checklist)Type: the department the checklist might belong to (Example: General, marketing, construction) Click Add Checklist.You should now see your new checklist name listed. Click the Add Field button to begin adding items.In the Add Custom Field window, enter a name for the field and select a field type. The types include different types of text, yes/no, and link to file/folder options. All of the field types are the same field types you can create when creating stand alone custom fields. Repeat the last step for all fields you would like to include on the checklist. Once all fields have been added, navigate to the Updates tab of a project to add the checklist.Under the Checklists section, click on Add Checklist.In the Add Checklist window, choose your new checklist name from the dropdown and create a unique Nickname for it. This is the name it will show as for this project. Having the ability to add a nickname allows the same checklist to be used multiple times within the same project. You can also add contributors. Contributors are users that are assigned to a Todo, which instructs them to help complete a checklist.You should now see your checklist listed in the checklist index below. Clicking on the checklist name will open a window which consists of your checklist fields. These can now be filled out. Once complete, click Save. All fields do not have to be filled out before saving. After saving, the checklist should now show a name and date under 'Last Updated By' as well as the progress percentage. This example shows that it is 67% complete because the dollar amount field was left blank.If we then go back into the checklist and complete all fields and Save, the progress will change to 100% and if you open the checklist back up, it will now show who completed it and the date next to the task.Checklists can also be linked to a tab within a project or to an individual document.To link to a tab, first go to the tab. We will choose the Construction tab for this example. In the Custom Fields section at the bottom, click Add Custom Field. Choose a name for the field and choose Link to Checklist from the Field Type dropdown.The checklist is now listed under Custom Fields. To add the checklist, click Edit and then Link to Checklist. Select your checklist from the dropdown and click Save.Now, click 'Edit Checklist' and then the checklist name will appear, clicking it will open up the checklist we added on the Updates tab.As mentioned earlier, you can also link a checklist to a document. To do this, go to the Files tab within the project and click on the file you want to attach the checklist to. In the File overview screen, click on the 'Connect Checklist' link in the File Details section on the right. Select the project name and the proper checklist from the corresponding drop-downs and Save.The checklist name should now show where the previous Connect Checklist link was located.Clicking this link will bring up the checklist that was originally created.For additional information on the Checklist Builder, check out the Checklist Builder subject category here.

180.subject: Admin Modules
180.title: Link new project to existing project folder tree
180.text: This feature is only available for a newly created project to share the folder tree of another already created project. You cannot choose to use/share another project's folder tree after creation. This process must be done on creation of a new project.When sharing a folder tree with another project, you’ll share every file. That means project photos, signed documents, etc. This does not share things like the Budget, Pay Apps, Tenants, and other project specific items. To create a project, sharing an already existing projects’ folder tree:Head to the global project page, and click ‘Add Project’Add project details as normal, and then click next. You’ll see this screen. Click the checkbox: ‘Link to Master Folder Tree’.From here, the modal will give you the option to choose a ‘master’ project. This basically means you’ll be sharing their folder tree. That means project photos, and all other files uploaded from one project, will be visible to the other. Once the project is created, you’ll be able to use it as normal. You’ll have access to the master project’s folder tree and all of it’s files. NOTE: When you delete a ‘borrowing’ project, it will delete it’s files from the shared template. As of now, you cannot delete a ‘master’ project. Once a project has been linked to another, you will be able to tell in the upper part of the project, beneath the project name. There is a chain link symbol, with the name of the master project next to it. If you click that, you'll be taken to the master project.
